<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{example-jetscheme}
	Let $X = \operatorname{Spec} (k[x,y]/(xy))$, two lines glued at the origin. If $A$ is a local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, an \emph{$A$-valued arc} is a map $\operatorname{Spec} (A[[t]]) \to X$. In our example, this corresponds to choosing two formal power series $f,g \in A[[t]]$ such that $f g = 0$. We can easily see that the functor sending a $k$-algebra to its space of arcs in $X$ is representable by the scheme
	\begin{align*}
		J := \operatorname{Spec}(k[a_0, a_1, \dots, b_0, b_1, \dots]/(c_0, c_1, \dots))
	\end{align*}
	where $c_i = \sum_{j= 0}^i a_j b_{i -j}$.

	Let $A_\infty := k[a_0, a_1, \dots, b_0, b_1, \dots]/(c_0, c_1, \dots)$ and let $I = (a_0, a_1, \dots, b_0, b_1)$. The trivial $k$-valued arc (that is, $f = g = 0$) is given by the natural map $A_\infty \to A_\infty/I \cong k$. This factorises through the ring $A_\infty/I^n$, which is a nilpotent thickening of $k$. This factorisation corresponds precisely to a deformation of this arc. Additionally, the map $A_\infty \to A_\infty/I^n$ cannot be written as a filtered colimit of maps $A_\infty \to B_i$, where $B_i$ is local and Artinian.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a ring with a fixed map $R \to k$. We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ for the $\infty$-category of animated $R$-algebras, and $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ for the $\infty$-category of animated $R$-algebras equipped with a compatible map to $k$.

	Finally, let $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ be the full subcategory of those $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ such that $\pi_0 (A) \to k$ is surjective.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- defi-1: body_md -->
An animated ring $A \in  \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ is \emph{local and Artinian} if
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $\pi_0 (A)$ is local and Artinian with residue field $k$.
		\item $\pi_i (A) \cong 0$ for $i \gg 0$.
		\item $\pi_i (A)$ is a finitely generated $\pi_0 (A)$-module for all $i$.
	\end{enumerate}
	We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{art}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ for the full subcategory of local and Artinian algebras.
<!-- end defi-1 -->
<!-- defi-2: body_md -->
An \emph{$R/k$ formal moduli problem} is a functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{art}} \to \mathcal{S}$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the $\infty$-category of spaces, such that
	\begin{itemize}
		\item $F(k) \simeq *$.
		\item $F$ preserves $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks.
	\end{itemize}
<!-- end defi-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories between $R/k$ formal moduli problems and partition Lie algebroids.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
Given any animated $k$-algebra $B$ equipped with a map $B \to k$, we have a $k/k$ formal moduli problem given by the functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (B, -)$. Following \cref{example-jetscheme}, the deformations of the trivial $k$-valued jet on $X$ are given by $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A_\infty, -)$. The associated partition Lie algebra has chain complex $L_{k/A_\infty}^\vee [1]$.

	An important insight is that this chain complex has a natural \emph{topological structure}. That is, $L_{k/A_\infty}$ is not finite, so its dual can be written as an inverse limit of finite type chain complexes. We must replace $k$-vector spaces with a suitable topological analogue.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop-nicesoliddescription}
	If $k = \mathbb{Q}$ or $\mathbb{F}_p$, the category of solid $k$-modules admits compact projective generators of the form $\prod_I k$, where $I$ is any set.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- defi-3: body_md -->
We write $\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k ^\omega)$ for the pro-completion (\cite{categories}, Definition 6.1.1) of finite-dimensional vector spaces. This is the category obtained by formally adding cofiltered limits to $\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega$. By duality, this is equivalent to $\operatorname{Vect}_k ^\text{op}$, so its objects are of the form $\prod_I k$ for some set $I$ and $\operatorname{Hom} (\prod_I k, k) = \bigoplus_I k$. The product $\prod_I k$ carries a profinite structure by writing it as $\varprojlim _{J \subset I} \bigoplus_J k$, where the limit is taken over all finite subsets of $I$.

	The category $\operatorname{Solid}_k ^\heartsuit$ of \emph{ultrasolid $k$-modules} is the ($1$-categorical) sifted cocompletion (\cite{sifted}, \S 2) of $\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)$. That is, $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\heartsuit$ is the category obtained by freely adding filtered colimits and reflexive coequalizers to $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)$. This can be identified with finite-product-preserving functors $(\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega))^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{Ab}$ that satisfy a left Kan extension condition (\cite{ultrasolid}, Definition 2.4).

	We will write $\operatorname{Solid}_k$ for the $\infty$-category of chain complexes of ultrasolid modules.
<!-- end defi-3 -->
<!-- defi-4: body_md -->
An object $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ is \emph{bounded and nilpotent} if
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $\pi_i (A) \cong 0$ for $i \gg 0$.
		\item $\pi_0 (A) \twoheadrightarrow k$ is surjective and $\mathfrak{m} := \ker (\pi_0 (A) \to k)$ is nilpotent; that is, $\mathfrak{m}^n = 0$ for $n \gg 0$.
	\end{enumerate}
	We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ for the full subcategory of bounded and nilpotent algebras.
<!-- end defi-4 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{example-sqz}
	Given $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}$, we can define the \emph{trivial square-zero extension} $k \oplus V$. That is, an animated ring whose underlying chain complex is $k \oplus V$ with trivial multiplication on $V$. If $V$ is eventually coconnective and not of finite type, the animated ring $k \oplus V$ is bounded and nilpotent but not Artinian.

	By the universal property of the cotangent complex, for any $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$, there is an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, k \oplus V) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_k} (L_{A/R} \otimes_A k, V)
	\end{align*}
	Thus, for any map $\alpha: L_{k/R}[-1] \to V$, we can define the \emph{square-zero extension} as the pullback diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			k \oplus_\alpha V \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & k \arrow{d}{\alpha} \\
			k \arrow{r}{0} & k \oplus V[1]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	We have that $\operatorname{fib} (k \oplus_\alpha V \to k) \simeq V$, and there is trivial multiplication on this fibre. Hence, if $V$ is eventually coconnective, $k \oplus_\alpha V$ is bounded and nilpotent, but not Artinian unless $V$ is of finite type.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- defi-5: body_md -->
A \emph{nilpotent formal moduli problem} is a functor $F : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $F(k) \simeq *$.
		\item $F$ preserves $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks.
		\item $F$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some cardinal $\kappa$.
	\end{enumerate}
	We will write $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$ for the $\infty$-category of nilpotent formal moduli problems.
<!-- end defi-5 -->
<!-- construction-1: body_md -->
\label{construction-tangentcomplex}
	Let $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ be a nilpotent formal moduli problem. Write $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty} \subset \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}$ for the full subcategory of eventually coconnective chain complexes. We have a functor
	\begin{align*}
		T_{k/F}[1] : (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/} \to \mathcal{S}
	\end{align*}
	given by
	\begin{align*}
		(L_{k/R}[-1] \xrightarrow{\alpha} V) \mapsto F(k \oplus_\alpha V	)
	\end{align*}
	that is accessible and preserves $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks. We can identify $T_{k/F}[1] $ with an object in $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ (\cref{lemma-cotcomplexasfunctor}), which we will call the \emph{tangent complex} of $F$.
<!-- end construction-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
The tangent complex (\cref{construction-tangentcomplex}) refines to an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		T_{k/-} [1] : \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
We will (informally) justify the connection between formal moduli problems and partition Lie algebroids. The square-zero extension in \cref{example-sqz} gives a functor $\operatorname{sqz}: (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$. This admits a left adjoint $\cot : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} \to (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1] /}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		A \mapsto (L_{k/R}[-1] \to L_{k/A}[-1])
	\end{align*}
	We can describe $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ as the smallest subcategory that contains the essential image of $\operatorname{sqz} : (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ and is closed under $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks. Given that formal moduli problems commute with $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks, all values of a formal moduli problem can be computed by knowing the values at square-zero extensions and the maps between them. By the adjunction,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (k \oplus_\alpha V , k \oplus_\beta W) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Mod}_k)_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}} (\cot(k \oplus_\alpha V), W)
	\end{align*}
	so we will be interested in the comonad $\cot \circ \operatorname{sqz} $ on $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$. Dualising, this gives a monad on $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, where $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}} \subset \operatorname{Solid}_k$ is the full subcategory of coconnective chain complexes with profinite homology. We will show that this uniquely extends to a sifted-colimit-preserving monad on $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, which is precisely the partition Lie algebroid monad.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- construction-2: body_md -->
For any $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, we will construct an $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ satisfying the following properties:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of surjections of discrete $R$-algebras $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ such that $\mathfrak{m}  = \ker (A \to B)$ satisfies $\mathfrak{m}^{n+1} = 0$. Then, there is a fully faithful embedding $\mathcal{C} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, and the image of this embedding generates $\operatorname{CAlg}_R ^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ under sifted colimits.
		\item $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq \infty} \simeq \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$, the $\infty$-category of arrows of animated $R$-algebras that are $\pi_0$-surjective.
		\item There is a monadic forgetful functor $\iota_n^\infty: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$. An object $(A \to B)$ in its essential image satisfies that for any classes $x_1, \dots, x_{n+1} \in \pi_* (\operatorname{fib} (A \to B))$, we have $x_1 \dots x_{n+1} = 0$ (although this is not a sufficient condition). Thus, we can informally think of objects in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ as arrows of animated rings such that the fibre is $(n+1)$-nilpotent, with extra structure expressing the coherence conditions for this nilpotence.
		\item More generally, if $m < n$, there is a monadic right adjoint $\iota_m^n : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. Informally, an $(m+1)$-nilpotent map is $(n+1)$-nilpotent.
		\item For $n < \infty$, there is a comonadic adjunction $\cot_{\leq n} : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}: \operatorname{sqz} $.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end construction-2 -->
<!-- construction-3: body_md -->
For each $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, we will construct a sifted-colimit-preserving monad $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$ on $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ satisfying the following properties:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The restriction of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$ to $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ is the monad $\cot_{\leq n}  ^\vee \circ \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)$.
		\item If $L_{k/R}$ is of finite type, the monad $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi := \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} \infty}$ restricted to $(\operatorname{Mod}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} \subset (\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ coincides with the partition Lie algebroid monad as defined in \cite{partition} and \cite{foliations}.
		\item For $m < n$, there is a map of monads $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$, which assembles into an equivalence of monads
			\begin{align*}
				\varinjlim_n \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \simeq \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi}
			\end{align*}
			and hence an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
			\begin{align*}
				\varprojlim_n \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} \simeq \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}
			\end{align*}
			where $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}$ is the category of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }}  n}$-algebras on $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end construction-3 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ be a map such that $\operatorname{fib} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is eventually coconnective and $\ker (\pi_0 (A) \to \pi_0 (B))$ is nilpotent. Then, $\operatorname{adic} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is complete.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- defi-6: body_md -->
Let $N(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})$ be the nerve of the poset $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. The category of \emph{filtered objects in $\mathcal{C}$} is defined as
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C}) := \operatorname{Fun} (N(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^{\text{op}}, \mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	Given a filtered object $X \in \operatorname{Fil}(\mathcal{C})$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, we will often write $F^i X := X(i)$.
<!-- end defi-6 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
If $\mathcal{C}$ is presentably symmetric monoidal, we can endow $\operatorname{Fil}(\mathcal{C})$ with a symmetric monoidal structure given by Day convolution, where we are using the additive monoidal structure on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- defi-7: body_md -->
Fix $n > 0$. We will write
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C}) := \operatorname{Fun} (\{0 \to \dots \to n \}^{\text{op}}, \mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	Notice that we have a fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C}) \subset \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C})$ whose essential image is given by those $X \in \operatorname{Fil}(\mathcal{C})$ such that $X(i) \simeq 0$ for $i > n$.
<!-- end defi-7 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
We can identify $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ with a localisation of $\operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C})$ whose kernel consists of $X \in \operatorname{Fil}(\mathcal{C})$ such that $\operatorname{Gr}^i (X) \simeq 0$ for $i\leq n$, so the left adjoint localisation functor inverts those maps inducing an equivalence in the first $n$ parts of the associated graded.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
\label{rem-filmonoidal}
	We can endow $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ with the structure of a symmetric monoidal category. Write $(-)_{\leq n} : \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C}) \to \operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ for the localisation functor.

	The kernel of this localisation is an ideal, so by (\cite{HA}, Proposition 2.2.1.9), we can endow $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ with a symmetric monoidal structure $\otimes^{\leq n}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		X \otimes^{\leq n} Y \simeq (X \otimes Y) _{\leq n}
	\end{align*}
	which makes the localisation functor symmetric monoidal.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- defi-8: body_md -->
Let $N(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{\operatorname{ds}})$ be the category indexed by the non-negative integers with only identity morphisms. The category of \emph{graded objects in $\mathcal{C}$} is defined as
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C}) := \operatorname{Fun} (N(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{\operatorname{ds}}), \mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	Given a graded object $X \in \operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, we will often write $X_i := X(i)$.
<!-- end defi-8 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
Similar to filtered objects, if $\mathcal{C}$ is symmetric monoidal, we can endow $\operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$ with a symmetric monoidal structure given by Day convolution, where we are using the additive monoidal structure on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{\operatorname{ds}}$. Given $X,Y \in \operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$,
	\begin{align*}
		(X \otimes Y)_i \simeq \bigoplus_{j + k = i} X_j \otimes Y_k
	\end{align*}
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- defi-9: body_md -->
Fix $n > 0$. We will write
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C}) := \operatorname{Fun} (\{0, \dots, n \}, \mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	There is a fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{Gr}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C}) \to \operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$, whose essential image is given by those $X \in \operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$ such that $X_i \simeq 0$ for $i > n$.
<!-- end defi-9 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
Just as in \cref{rem-filmonoidal}, $\operatorname{Gr}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ can be endowed with a symmetric monoidal structure through localisation. This is essentially the symmetric monoidal product on $\operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})$ where we discard anything in degree $> n$.
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- defi-10: body_md -->
We say $X \in \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C})$ is \emph{complete} if $\varprojlim F^i X \simeq 0$.

	Given $X \in \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C})$, we have an \emph{associated graded} $\operatorname{Gr} (X)$ defined as
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr}(X)_i := \operatorname{cofib} (F^{i+1} X \to F^i X)
	\end{align*}
	This gives a symmetric monoidal functor
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr} : \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C}) \to \operatorname{Gr} (\mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	which restricts to a symmetric monoidal functor
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr}: \operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C}) \to \operatorname{Gr}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
<!-- end defi-10 -->
<!-- rem-7: body_md -->
If $X, Y \in \operatorname{Fil} (\mathcal{C})$ are complete, the map $X \to Y$ is an equivalence if and only if the map $\operatorname{Gr} (X) \to \operatorname{Gr}(Y)$ is an equivalence.

	Given $X,Y \in \operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$, they are obviously complete, so equivalences in $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} (\mathcal{C})$ are detected by the associated gradeds.
<!-- end rem-7 -->
<!-- defi-11: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a poset. Then, we can construct a simplicial set $\Delta (P)$ as follows: the $n$-simplices of $\Delta(P)$ are chains $x_0 \leq \dots \leq x_n$ in $P$. Face maps delete elements in the chain, and degeneracy maps insert repeated elements in the chain.

	We will not generally distinguish between $\Delta(P)$ and its geometric realisation.
<!-- end defi-11 -->
<!-- defi-12: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a poset. We say that $P$ is \emph{atomised} if every element of $P$ lies above some minimal element and every finite set of minimal elements with an upper bound has a join.

	If $P$ is atomised, we call its minimal elements atoms and we will denote the set of atoms by $\mathcal{A} (P)$. We will say that a subset $S \subset  \mathcal{A}(P)$ \emph{generates $P$} if $P_{\geq S}$ is empty.
<!-- end defi-12 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop-atomised}
	Let $P$ be an atomised poset such that no $k$ atoms generate it. Then, $\Delta(P)$ is $(k-2)$-connected.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- defi-13: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a topological space. Then, its \emph{unreduced suspension} $X^\diamond$ is the topological space $(X\times \Delta^1)/_{\stackrel{(x,0)\sim (x',0)}{_{(x,1)\sim (x',1)}}}$.
<!-- end defi-13 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{prop-unreduced}
	Let $P$ be a poset, and let $\tilde{P} := P \cup \{\hat{1}\}$, where $\hat{1} \geq x$ for all $x \in P$. Then, $\Delta(P)^\diamond$ is homotopy equivalent to the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are given by
	\begin{align*}
		\{x_0 \leq \dots \leq x_n = \hat{1} | x_i \in \tilde{P} \} \bigsqcup \{*\}
	\end{align*}
	The face maps preserve the basepoint and delete elements in the chain, sending invalid chains to the basepoint. The degeneracy maps insert repeated elements in the chain.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- defi-14: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$. We will write $\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ for the $1$-category of pairs of $R$-algebras of the form
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \xrightarrow{V \mapsto 0} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	where $V,W$ are finite free $R$-modules, and $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V)$ is the free $R$-algebra on $V$ quotiented by the ideal generated by $V^{\otimes n+1}$.

	The category of \emph{animated $(n+1)$-nilpotent surjections of $R$-algebras} is the $\infty$-category
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} := \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n})
	\end{align*}
	In other words, this is the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun} ((\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^{\text{op}}, \mathcal{S})$ spanned by the finite-product-preserving functors.

	For $n = \infty$, we will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} := \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq \infty}$.
<!-- end defi-14 -->
<!-- rem-8: body_md -->
This definition is very much inspired by the category of \emph{animated surjections} as introduced in \cite{mao}. A map $R \to S$ of animated rings is an animated surjection if the map $\pi_0 (R) \to \pi_0 (S)$ is surjective. It turns out that this category is compactly generated by projectives of the form
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_\mathbb{Z}^* (V) \otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_\mathbb{Z}^* (W) \xrightarrow{V \mapsto 0} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_\mathbb{Z}^* (W) 
	\end{align*}
	where $V$ and $W$ are finite free abelian groups (\cite{mao}, Theorem 1.12).

	Hence, our construction gives a category of surjections where the fibre is $(n+1)$-nilpotent, but there are coherence conditions that restrict these maps. For example, for $n = 1$, write $(R \oplus Rx \oplus Ry \twoheadrightarrow R)$ for the free $2$-nilpotent surjection on generators $x$ and $y$ in degree zero. Any map of $2$-nilpotent surjections from $(R \oplus Rx \oplus Ry \twoheadrightarrow R)$ to $(R \oplus Rz \twoheadrightarrow R)$ (where $z$ is taken in homological degree $i > 0$) is trivial. For $n = \infty$, this mapping space describes the free partition Lie algebra on two generators, or, more classically, the André-Quillen cohomology of $k[x,y]/(x^2, y^2, xy)$.

	It will be useful to consider this category not as $(n+1)$-nilpotent surjections $A \twoheadrightarrow B$, but rather as pairs $(A,I)$ where $I$ is the kernel ideal of the surjection. This allows us to compute limits, since a limit of surjections might not be surjective.
<!-- end rem-8 -->
<!-- construction-4: body_md -->
\label{construction-forgetsurj}
	We will now construct a forgetful functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$. Informally, this will take a	surjection $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ to $\operatorname{fib} (A \to B) \to A$.

	Let $\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega)$ be the category of arrows of the form $V \xrightarrow{i} V \oplus W$, where $i$ is the canonical inclusion map. We will often call these \emph{standard arrows}. By (\cite{mao}, Corollary 2.13), $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}) \simeq \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega))$.

	We have a functor $\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega) \to \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		(V \mapsto V \oplus W) \mapsto (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* _R (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* _R(W) )
	\end{align*}
	Since it preserves coproducts, it induces a functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$ on these subcategories of presheaves by composition.
<!-- end construction-4 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop-surjmonadic}
	The functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,  \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$ from \cref{construction-forgetsurj} preserves sifted colimits and is monadic. It is given on $\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ by
	\begin{align*}
		\left( \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* _R (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \right) & \mapsto \\ 
																						 & \left(\bigoplus_{0 < i \leq n} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^i (V) \right) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) 
	\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
$F$ commutes with all limits and sifted colimits, since these are computed pointwise in $\mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\mathcal{C})$ for a small category $\mathcal{C}$ (where we consider $\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(\mathcal{C})$ as a subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun} (\mathcal{C}^{\text{op}}, \mathcal{S})$). Additionally, the functor $\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega) \to \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ is essentially surjective, so $F$ must be conservative.	The functor is then monadic by the crude version of the Barr-Beck-Lurie Theorem (\cite{HA}, Theorem 4.7.0.3).

	One can easily check that the functor is as given on compact projectives.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- construction-5: body_md -->
\label{construction-targetring}
	We have a sifted-colimit-preserving functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ given on compact projectives by
	\begin{align*}
		\left( \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \right) \mapsto \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	This also commutes with coproducts of compact projectives, so it commutes with all colimits. Informally, this is the functor $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \mapsto B$. We will often refer to this as the \emph{target ring}.
<!-- end construction-5 -->
<!-- rem-9: body_md -->
\label{rem-pairs}
	By \cref{prop-surjmonadic}, we can think of an object in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ as an arrow $I \to A$ in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ with the structure of a monad algebra. We will often write this as a pair $(A,I)$ (so the map $I \to A$ is omitted) or as an arrow $A \twoheadrightarrow B$, where $B := \operatorname{cofib} (I \to A)$. Notice that $B$ has the structure of an animated ring (\cref{construction-targetring}).

	We will later see that $A$ also has the structure of an animated ring, plus extra structure accounting for the nilpotence of the kernel ideal (\cref{prop-iotamonadic}).
<!-- end rem-9 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma-projfree}
	Let $V, W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$. Then, the object $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (W)$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj},\leq n}$ can be identified with the free algebra on $V \to V \oplus W$ with respect to the monad in \cref{prop-surjmonadic}.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj},\leq n}$. Then, we just need to establish an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (W) \to \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (W), A \to B) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R,	\geq 0})} (V \to V \oplus W, I \to A)
	\end{align*}
	where $I := \operatorname{fib} (A \to B)$.

	Notice that both sides commute with sifted colimits in the second variable due to the relevant objects being compact projective, so we only need to show this for $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj},\leq n}$, and then it is clear.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
We will abuse notation and write $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R : \operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}) \to \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$ for the monad coming from \cref{prop-surjmonadic}, and we will write the free algebra on an arrow $V \to W$ as $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to W)$. Notice that with this notation, for a standard arrow $V \to V \oplus W$ in $\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$,
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W) \simeq (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \xrightarrow{V \mapsto 0} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W))
	\end{align*}
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lemma-animatedsubcat}
	There is a fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{CAlg}^{\operatorname{an}}_R \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ given by the sifted-colimit-preserving extension of
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (V) \mapsto \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (0 \to V)
	\end{align*}
	for $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$. Its essential image are those $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ such that the map $A \to B$ is an equivalence of chain complexes.

	Additionally, for any $A \twoheadrightarrow B \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ and $C \xrightarrow{\simeq} C \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ there is an equivalence of arrows of chain complexes
	\begin{align*}
		(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \sqcup (C \xrightarrow{\simeq} C) \simeq (A \otimes_R C \twoheadrightarrow B \otimes_R C)
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The functor being fully faithful is a direct consequence of (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.5.8.22). Now suppose $(A \xrightarrow{\simeq} A) \in  \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. By its bar resolution, we can write it as a geometric realisation of objects in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R ^{\operatorname{an}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$.

	For the part about coproducts, since the forgetful functor commutes with sifted colimits, it is enough to show it for $C \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^*_R (U)$ and $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W)$ for $U,V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$. This follows from the fact that $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R : \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} ) \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ commutes with coproducts.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop-surjheart}
	Let $(\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}) ^{\heartsuit} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ be the full subcategory consisting of those $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ such that $A,B \in \operatorname{Mod}_R^\heartsuit$. Then, $(\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^\heartsuit$ is equivalent to the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{CAlg}_R^\heartsuit)$ consisting of those arrows $A \to B$ that are surjective in $\pi_0$ and the kernel ideal is $(n+1)$-nilpotent.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1, \operatorname{CAlg}_R^\heartsuit)$ be the full subcategory consisting of arrows $A \to B$ that are surjective and the kernel ideal is $(n+1)$-nilpotent.

	Then, the restriction of the Yoneda embedding gives us a functor $h: \mathcal{C} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. That is, $(A \to B) \mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{CAlg}_R^\heartsuit)} (-, A \to B)$. We first show that it is faithful. Consider two maps $f,g: (A \to B) \to (C \to D)$ in $\mathcal{C}$, which we can think of as maps $f,g: A \to C$ preserving the kernel ideal. If these two maps are not the same, there is some $a \in A$ such that $f(a) \neq g(a)$.

	We have a natural identification $h(A \to B) (R[x] \to R[x]) \cong A$ and $h(C \to D) (R[x] \to R[x]) \cong C$. The natural transformations $h(f)$ and $h(g)$ at the element $(R[x] \to R[x])$ simply reduce to the maps $f,g$, so it follows that $h(f) \neq h(g)$. Hence, $h$ is faithful.

	We will now show that it is full. Suppose we have a natural transformation $F: h(A \to B) \to h(C \to D)$. As before, $F$ at the value $(R[x] \to R[x])$ induces a map $f: A \to C$. Compatibility with the map $(R[x] \to R[x]) \to (R[x]/x^{n+1} \to R)$ ensures that this map preserves the kernel ideal. Additionally, compatibility with the maps $(R[x] \to R[x]) \xrightarrow{x \mapsto y +z} (R[y,z] \to R[y,z])$ and $(R[x] \to R[x]) \xrightarrow{x \mapsto yz} (R[y,z] \to R[y,z])$ implies that this is a ring map. It easily follows that $h(f) = F$.

	Finally, we prove that $h$ is essentially surjective on the category of objects $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are discrete. We first show that the object $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ is $0$-truncated. By the bar resolution, it suffices to show that $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n} (V \to W), (A \to B))$ is $0$-truncated, since $0$-truncated spaces are closed under limits. But this is clear since $I \to A$ is $0$-truncated in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$, where $I = \ker (A \to B)$.

	Now consider $(A \to B)$ as a functor $F: (\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^{\text{op}} \to \mathcal{S}$. Notice that for a standard arrow $V \to V \oplus W$, we have a natural identification $F(\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W), (A \to B))$. Since $(A \to B)$ is $0$-truncated, $F$ is a functor whose image is in $\operatorname{Set} \subset \mathcal{S}$.

	By \cref{construction-forgetsurj}, we can also identify $A \cong F(R[x] \to R[x])$ and $I \cong F(R[x]/x^{n+1} \to R)$, where $I = \operatorname{fib} (A \to B)$. Compatibility with the maps in $\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ endows $A$ with the structure of an $R$-algebra and $I$ with the structure of an $(n+1)$-nilpotent ideal. One can then easily check that this is precisely the Yoneda embedding of the constructed ring map.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- defi-15: body_md -->
Let $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$. We define the category $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ by the pullback diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & * \arrow{d}{* \mapsto S} \\
			\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{r}{\operatorname{target}} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Informally, it is the subcategory of $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ consisting of arrows of the form $A \twoheadrightarrow S$ and maps that reduce to the identity on the target ring.
<!-- end defi-15 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop-nonunital}
	The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ / R}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		(A \twoheadrightarrow R) \mapsto \operatorname{fib} (A \to R)
	\end{align*}
	is monadic. The relevant monad is given by the sifted-colimit-preserving monad given on $\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$ by
	\begin{align*}
		V \mapsto \bigoplus_{0 < i \leq n} V^{\otimes i}_{\Sigma _i}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The functor is clearly conservative and preserves sifted colimits, so it is monadic. For the last part, we can use \cref{lemma-projfree} to identify $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V)$ with the free algebra on $V$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- notation-3: body_md -->
We will write $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n}: \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \to \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the resulting monad. Sometimes, we will abuse notation and write $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n} (V)$ for the image of the free algebra on $V$ in the category $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. In other words, $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n} (V) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V)$.
<!-- end notation-3 -->
<!-- construction-6: body_md -->
\label{construction-polyomialtruncation}
	Let $m \leq n$. Then, there is a functor $t_{\leq m} ^n : \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W) \mapsto \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq m} _R (V \to V \oplus W)
	\end{align*}
	Informally, for an $(n+1)$-nilpotent surjection $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel ideal $I$, $t_{\leq m} ^n (A \twoheadrightarrow B) = (A/I^{m+1} \to B)$.

	Notice that by left Kan extending we get a colimit-preserving functor $t_{\leq m} ^n : \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$.

	We will write its right adjoint as $\iota_m ^n : \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. More explicitly, if $X \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$, we can write it as a finite-product-preserving functor $X: (\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m})^{\text{op}} \to \mathcal{S}$. Then, $\iota_m^n(X) : (\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n })^{\text{op}} \to \mathcal{S}$ is the composition of $X$ with $t_{\leq m}^n : \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$.

	Notice that sifted colimits of product-preserving functors are computed pointwise, so the functor $\iota_m^n$ commutes with sifted colimits.
<!-- end construction-6 -->
<!-- rem-10: body_md -->
\label{rem-iotapreservesmodule}
	Consider the functor $\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega) \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ from \cref{construction-forgetsurj}. Then, there is a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{Arr}^{\operatorname{st}} (\operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega) \arrow{dr} \arrow{r} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{d}{t_{\leq m}^n} \\
																			 & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	By the definition of these functors, this implies that there is a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \arrow{r}{\iota_m ^n} \arrow{dr}[swap]{\operatorname{forget}} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{d}{\operatorname{forget}} \\
																									& \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	So the functor $\iota_m^n$ preserves the underlying arrow of modules. Due to this, when it is clear from context, we will omit the functor $\iota_m^n$. That is, given $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$, we will write $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ for $\iota_m^n (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$.
<!-- end rem-10 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop-iotamonadic}
	Let $m \leq n$. The functor $\iota_m^n$ is monadic.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By \cref{rem-iotapreservesmodule}, $\iota_m^n$ preserves the underlying arrow in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$. Since the forgetful functor is conservative, $\iota_m^n$ is conservative. It also commutes with all sifted colimits, so by the crude version of the Barr-Beck-Lurie Theorem (\cite{HA}, Theorem 4.7.0.3) we are done.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- rem-11: body_md -->
In particular, setting $n = \infty$, we have a monadic functor $\iota_m^\infty: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq \infty}$. The latter is just the category of animated surjections, supporting our earlier claim that an object $A \twoheadrightarrow B$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ is just an animated surjection with $(m+1)$-nilpotent kernel ideal and extra structure accounting for the coherence conditions of the nilpotence.
<!-- end rem-11 -->
<!-- rem-12: body_md -->
The functors $\iota_m^n: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ preserve the underlying modules, so by \cref{prop-surjheart} they restrict to functors $\iota_m^n: (\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m})^\heartsuit \to (\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^\heartsuit$. 

	This corresponds to the functor sending a surjective map of rings $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ with $(m+1)$-nilpotent kernel ideal to itself; that is, an $(m+1)$-nilpotent ideal is necessarily $(n+1)$-nilpotent.
<!-- end rem-12 -->
<!-- rem-13: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ be the full subcategory generated under coproducts by objects of the form $R^{\leq i}$ where $F^j R^{\leq i} \simeq 0$ for $j > i$ and $F^j R^{\leq i} \simeq R$ for $j \leq i$. In other words, $\operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ is the subcategory of finitely generated free filtered $R$-modules where each generator is of a certain filtered weight. By (\cite{mao}, Corollary 2.13), $\operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \simeq \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$.
<!-- end rem-13 -->
<!-- notation-4: body_md -->
We will write $\operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the full subcategory of finite free modules in filtered weight $0$.

	We will write $\operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}}^{\geq 1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the full subcategory of finite free modules all of whose generators are in filtered weight $ > 0$. Note that this is spanned under coproducts by objects of the form $R^{\leq i}$ where $i > 0$.
<!-- end notation-4 -->
<!-- defi-16: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$. We will write $\operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$ for the category of filtered rings of the form $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)$, where $V \in \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}} ^{\geq 1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$.

	The category of \emph{animated filtered $(n+1)$-nilpotent surjections} is
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} := \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n})
	\end{align*}
<!-- end defi-16 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sifted-colimit-preserving extension of the forgetful functor $\operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n} \to \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ is monadic. We will write $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil},\leq n}$ for the resulting monad.
		\item Given $V \in \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}}^{\geq 1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Fil}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$, we can identify $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)$ with the free $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil}, \leq n}$-algebra on $V \oplus W$.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- construction-7: body_md -->
Notice that there is a fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \subset \operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$, where for $V, W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$, we identify $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W)$ with $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil}, \leq n} (V \oplus W)$, where we consider $V$ in filtered weight $1$ and $W$ in filtered weight $0$. Notice that this embedding commutes with finite coproducts.

	By (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.5.8.22 and Proposition 5.5.8.15), there is a fully faithful colimit-preserving embedding $\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} : \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, which we will call the \emph{adic filtration}. Notice that $F^j \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n}(-) \simeq 0$ for $j > n$.

	This admits a right adjoint $\operatorname{aug}: \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$.
<!-- end construction-7 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
Let $R \in \operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$. Then, there is an isomorphism of arrows of chain complexes
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{aug} (R) \simeq (F^0 R, F^1 R)
	\end{align*}
	where we use the notation of \cref{rem-pairs}.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
For a standard arrow $V \to V \oplus W$, we have natural equivalences
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})} (V \to V \oplus W, \operatorname{aug}(R)) & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W), \operatorname{aug} (R)) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n}}_R (V \to V \oplus W), R) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}} (V \to V \oplus W, R) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})} (V \to V \oplus W, F^1 R \to F^0 R)
	\end{align*}
	Since all of the mapping spaces commute with sifted colimits in the first variable, this is true for all $V \to W$ in $\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$. We are now done by the Yoneda embedding.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- defi-17: body_md -->
We will write $\operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the full subcategory generated under coproducts by graded modules of the form $R^i$, where $R^i_j \simeq 0$ for $i \neq j$ and $R^i_j \simeq R$ for $i = j$. In other words, these are the finitely generated free graded modules where each generator is homogeneous of a fixed degree.

	We will write $\operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the category of finitely generated free graded modules in degree $0$. Similarly, we will write $\operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^{\geq  1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ for the finitely generated free graded modules such that every generator is homogeneous of degree $> 0$.
<!-- end defi-17 -->
<!-- defi-18: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$. We will write $\operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$ for the category of graded algebras of the form $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)$, where $V \in \operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^{\geq 1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$.

	The category of \emph{animated graded $(n+1)$-nilpotent surjections} is
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} := \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n})
	\end{align*}
<!-- end defi-18 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sifted-colimit-preserving extension of the forgetful functor $\operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ is monadic. We will write $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Gr},\leq n}$ for the resulting monad.
		\item Given $V \in \operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^{\geq 1} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Gr}_{\operatorname{free}}^0 \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$, we can identify $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)$ with the free $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n}$-algebra on $V \oplus W$.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- defi-19: body_md -->
We will write $\operatorname{Gr} : \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ for the sifted-colimit-preserving extension of the functor $\operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$ that takes the associated graded.
<!-- end defi-19 -->
<!-- defi-20: body_md -->
We will write $\operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{Mod}$ for the $\infty$-category of pairs $(A,M)$ where $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ and $M \in \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_A$. We can construct this as the source of the biCartesian fibration that classifies the functor $A \mapsto \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_A$

	Similarly, let $\operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{Mod}$ be the $\infty$-category of pairs $(A,M)$ where $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ and $M \in \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Mod}_A$.
<!-- end defi-20 -->
<!-- defi-21: body_md -->
We construct a functor $\cot_{\leq n} : \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}$ and $\cot_{\leq n} : \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{Mod}$. Suppose $ A \in \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$ or $\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Poly}_R^{\leq n}$. Then define
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (A) := (\operatorname{Gr}^0 (A), I/I^2)
	\end{align*}
	where $I:= \operatorname{fib} (A \to \operatorname{Gr}^0 (A))$. If $V \in \operatorname{Fil}^{> 0}_{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Fil}^0 _{\operatorname{free}} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$, this gives $\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil}, \leq n} (V \oplus W)) \simeq (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W), \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \otimes_R V)$, and similar for the graded analogue.

	This clearly commutes with coproducts, so by (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.5.8.15) we get a colimit-preserving functor $\cot_{\leq n} : \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}$ and $\cot_{\leq n} : \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Mod}$. Notice that in both cases we get $\operatorname{Gr}^0 \cot_{\leq n} (-) \simeq 0$.
<!-- end defi-21 -->
<!-- rem-14: body_md -->
By checking on compact projectives one has that for any $A' \in \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr} (\cot_{\leq n} (A')) & \simeq \cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Gr} (A')) \\
		\operatorname{aug} (\cot_{\leq n} (A')) & \simeq \cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{aug} (A')) \\
	\end{align*}
<!-- end rem-14 -->
<!-- construction-8: body_md -->
Just as in the non-filtered case, for $m \leq n$ we have polynomial truncation adjunctions $t_{\leq m}^n: \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows \operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} : \iota_m^n$ and $t_{\leq m}^n : \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows \operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} : \iota_m^n$. The functors $\iota_m^n$ preserve the underlying filtered/graded module, and for $V \in \operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and $W \in \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$,
	\begin{align*}
		t_{\leq m} ^n (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil}, \leq n} (V)) & \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Fil}, \leq m} (V) \\
		t_{\leq m}^n (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n} (W)) & \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq m} (W)
	\end{align*}
<!-- end construction-8 -->
<!-- defi-22: body_md -->
We will write $\operatorname{Mod}$ for the $\infty$-category of pairs $(A,M)$ where $A$ is an animated $R$-algebra and $M$ is an $A$-module. A map $(A,M) \to (B,N)$ is given by a map of animated $R$-algebras $A \to B$ and a map of modules $B \otimes_A M \to N$.

	Let $\operatorname{Mod}_{\geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Mod}$ be the full subcategory spanned by the pairs $(A,M)$ where $M$ is connective. Then, we can write $\operatorname{Mod}_{\geq 0} := \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (\operatorname{PolyMod})$, where $\operatorname{PolyMod}$ is the subcategory of pairs $(\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (V), \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (V) \otimes_R W)$, where $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$.
<!-- end defi-22 -->
<!-- construction-9: body_md -->
We construct a functor 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{triv}: \operatorname{Mod}_{\geq 0} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}
	\end{align*}
	We define it as the sifted-colimit-preserving extension of the functor $\operatorname{PolyMod} \to (\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^\heartsuit \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ sending a pair $(A,M)$ to the surjection $A \oplus M \twoheadrightarrow A$, where $A \oplus M$ has trivial multiplicative structure on $M$. For $m \leq n$, we get a commutative diagram of sifted-colimit-preserving functors
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{Mod} \arrow{dr}[swap]{\operatorname{triv}} \arrow{r}{\operatorname{triv}} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \arrow{d}{\iota_m^n} \\
																						 & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The forgetful functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0})$ commutes with sifted colimits, so by definition we have that the underlying pair of $\operatorname{triv} (A,M)$ is $(M, A \oplus M)$.

	This implies that $\operatorname{triv}$ commutes with limits, since limits are computed in the underlying module. Hence, it has a left adjoint which we will write as $L^{\leq n}: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Mod}$.
<!-- end construction-9 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
Let $V,W \in \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		L^{\leq n}(\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W), (V \oplus W) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) )
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Given $(B,M) \in \operatorname{Mod}$, we have a natural equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Mod}} (L^{\leq n}(\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W)), (B,M)) & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an} , \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W), B\oplus M \to B) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}_R)} (V \to V \oplus W, M \to B \oplus M) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_R} (V, M) \times \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Mod}_R} (W, B \oplus M) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}} ((\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W), (V \oplus W) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)), (B,M))
	\end{align*}
	so we are done by the Yoneda embedding.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- rem-15: body_md -->
For $n = \infty$, the functor $L^{\leq n}: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} \to \operatorname{Mod}$ is the functor $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \mapsto (B, L_{A/R} \otimes_A B)$.
<!-- end rem-15 -->
<!-- defi-23: body_md -->
The $\infty$-category of \emph{derivations} is the $\infty$-category defined by the pullback diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{Der}_{/R} \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1, \operatorname{Mod}) \times _{\operatorname{Fun} (\Delta^1, \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}})} \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}} \arrow{d}{\operatorname{ev}_0} \\
			\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}} \arrow{r}{L_{-/R}[-1]} & \operatorname{Mod}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	In other words, this is the category of triples $(B, M,\alpha)$, where $B$ is an animated $R$-algebra, $M$ is a $B$-module and $\alpha: L_{B/R}[-1] \to M$ is a map of $B$-modules.

	Given $B \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$, we will write $\operatorname{Der}_{B/R}$ for the $\infty$-category defined by the following pullback square.
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{Der}_{B/R} \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \operatorname{Der}_{/R} \arrow{d} \\
			* \arrow{r}{* \mapsto B} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Note that we have an equivalence $\operatorname{Der}_{B/R} \simeq (\operatorname{Mod}_B)_{L_{B/R}[-1]/}$.

	The map $\operatorname{Der}_{/R} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ is a biCartesian fibration, classifying the functor $A \mapsto \operatorname{Der}_{A/R}$. Given a map $f: A \to B$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$, this induces a right adjoint $f_*: \operatorname{Der}_{B/R} \to \operatorname{Der}_{A/R}$ by restriction of scalars. That is, given a derivation $\beta : L_{B/R}[-1] \to M$, we have a  map of $A$-modules $L_{A/R}[-1] \to L_{B/R}[-1] \to M$. Its left adjoint is given on a derivation $\alpha: L_{A/R}[-1] \to M$ by the pushout of the following diagram of $B$-modules
	\begin{align*}
		L_{B/R}[-1]  \leftarrow B \otimes_A L_{A/R}[-1] \xrightarrow{\alpha} B \otimes_A M
	\end{align*}
<!-- end defi-23 -->
<!-- construction-10: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{Der}_{/R, \geq -1} \subset \operatorname{Der}_{/R}$ be the full subcategory spanned by pairs $(A,L_{A/R}[-1] \to M)$ where $M$ is a $(-1)$-connective $A$-module. We will abuse notation and write $\operatorname{triv}[1]: \operatorname{Der}_{/R, \geq -1} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ given by $(B,\alpha: L_{B/R}[-1] \to M) \mapsto \operatorname{triv} (B, M[1]) \simeq (B \oplus M[1] \twoheadrightarrow B)$. This factors through the forgetful  map $\operatorname{Der}_{/R} \to \operatorname{Mod}$, whose left adjoint maps a pair $(B,M)$ to the derivation $(B, L_{B/R}[-1] \to L_{B/R}[-1] \oplus M)$. Hence, we get a left adjoint 
	\begin{align*}
		(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \mapsto (B, \alpha: L_{B/R}[-1] \to L_{B/R}[-1] \oplus L^{\leq n}(A \twoheadrightarrow B)[-1])
	\end{align*}
	The forgetful map $\operatorname{const}: \operatorname{Der}_{/R} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ given by $(A, \alpha: L_{A/R}[-1] \to M) \mapsto (A \xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}} A)$, has a left adjoint given by $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \mapsto (B, L_{B/R}[-1] \xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}} L_{B/R}[-1])$.

	Note that
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}} (B \to B, B \oplus M[1] \to B) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_B} (L_{B/R}, M[1]) 
	\end{align*}
	Hence, given a derivation $(B, \alpha: L_{B/R}[-1] \to M)$, there are two canonical maps $(B \to B) \to (B \oplus M[1] \to B)$, one given by $\alpha$ and the other one given by zero. This gives two natural transformations $0, \alpha: \operatorname{const} \to \operatorname{triv}[1]$. We will write $\operatorname{sqz}: \operatorname{Der}_{/R, \leq -1} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ for the functor defined by the pullback diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{sqz} \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \operatorname{const} \arrow{d}{\alpha} \\
			\operatorname{const} \arrow{r}{0} & \operatorname{triv}[1]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Since $\operatorname{sqz}$ is a pullback of right adjoints, it is a right adjoint. We will write $\cot_{\leq n}: \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Der}_{/R, \geq -1}$ for its left adjoint, which can be written as a pushout of the left adjoints.

	We will sometimes abuse notation and, given $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, we will still write $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ for the underlying module after forgetting the derivation.
<!-- end construction-10 -->
<!-- rem-16: body_md -->
For $n = \infty$, this is the functor $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \mapsto (L_{B/R}[-1] \to L_{B/A}[-1])$.
<!-- end rem-16 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
Let $m \leq n$. Since $\operatorname{sqz} \simeq \iota_m^n \circ \operatorname{sqz}$, we can deduce an analogous statement for the left adjoints. That is,
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} \simeq \cot_{\leq m} \circ t_{\leq m} ^n
	\end{align*}
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
Let $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$ and $n > 0$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W), W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1]  \xrightarrow{0} V \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W))
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
There is a pushout diagram in $\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) /R}$
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			(W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1] \xrightarrow{0} (V \oplus W) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1] ) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & ( W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1] \xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}} W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1]) \arrow{d} \\
			( W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1] \xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}} W \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)[-1]) \arrow{r} & \cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V \oplus W))
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	from which the result follows.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
In particular, we see that $\cot_{\leq n }$ always lands in connective modules, since connective modules are closed under sifted colimits. That is, it lands in $\operatorname{Der}_{/R, \geq 0} \subset \operatorname{Der}_{/R, \geq -1}$, the full subcategory spanned by those derivations $(B, \alpha: L_{B/R}[-1] \to M)$ where $M$ is connective.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
<!-- rem-19: body_md -->
By checking on compact projectives, we can see that for any $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ there is an equivalence	
	\begin{align*}
		F^{* \leq 1} \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) & \simeq \cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B))
	\end{align*}
	where $F^{* \leq 1} \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is the module $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ put in filtration weight $1$. In the above, we are forgetting the map from $L_{B/R}[-1]$ and considering $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ as an object in $\operatorname{Mod}_{B, \geq 0}$.
<!-- end rem-19 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lemma-gradic}
	There is a natural equivalence of functors $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{CAlg}_R ^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr} \circ \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_B^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n} (\cot^{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) (1))
	\end{align*}
	where $\cot^{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) (1)$ refers to the graded chain complex with $\cot^{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ concentrated in degree $1$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Both functors commute with sifted colimits, so it easily follows by computing both sides on compact projectives.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop-cotsplit}
	Let $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$. Let $X^\bullet$ be an augmented cosimplicial diagram in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ that is $\cot_{\leq n}$-split. Then, $\operatorname{Tot}(X^\bullet)$, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Tot}(X^\bullet)) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Tot} (\cot_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence, where the totalisation is computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_S$.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
$\operatorname{Gr}\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_S^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n} (\cot_{\leq n}(X^\bullet)(1))$ is also split and the totalisation, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_S$, is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$. The forgetful functor $\operatorname{Mod}_S \to \operatorname{Mod}_R$ commutes with limits, so this totalisation is also computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. This gives an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Tot} (\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)))
	\end{align*}
	where the totalisation is computed in $\operatorname{Gr}^{\leq n} \operatorname{Mod}_R$.

	$\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))$, computed in $\operatorname{Fil}^{\leq n} \operatorname{Mod}_R$, has graded $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))$. Additionally, for each $i < n$ there is an exact sequence
	\begin{align*}
		F^{i+1}\operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) \to F^i \operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) \to \operatorname{Gr}^i \operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))
	\end{align*}
	and $F^n \operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) \simeq \operatorname{Gr}^n \operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))$. By induction, we see that each filtered piece, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$, is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$. Additionally, there is a natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))) \to \operatorname{Tot} (\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))) 	
	\end{align*}
	The filtrations are finite and hence complete, and this is an equivalence after passing to gradeds, so it is an equivalence.

	We can now just take $\operatorname{aug}$ to conclude that $\operatorname{Tot}(X^\bullet)$, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$, is in $\operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$ and that the map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Tot}(X^\bullet)) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Tot}(\cot_{\leq n} (X^\bullet))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop-cotcomonadic}
	Let $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$. For $n < \infty$, the adjunction
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n}: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows (\operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0})_{L_{S/R}[-1]/}: \operatorname{sqz} 
	\end{align*}
	is comonadic.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
First we show that $\cot_{\leq n}$ is conservative. Suppose $A \to B$ is a map in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ inducing an equivalence on $\cot_{\leq n}$. Then, $\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (A\twoheadrightarrow S) \to \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (B \twoheadrightarrow S)$ is an equivalence on associated gradeds. By completeness, since these filtrations are finite, this is an equivalence before taking gradeds. The functor $\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n}$ is fully faithful, so $A \simeq B$.

	By \cref{prop-cotsplit}, $\cot_{\leq n}$-split cosimplicial diagrams commute with $\cot_{\leq n}$, so we are done by the Barr-Beck-Lurie Theorem (\cite{HA}, Theorem 4.4.3.5).
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- defi-24: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a discrete ring and $G$ a finite group. We will write $R[\mathcal{O}_G]$ for the $1$-category of discrete $R[G]$-modules of the form $R[S]$, where $S$ is a finite $G$-set. Note that every object in this category can be written as a coproduct of objects of the form $R[G/H]$, where $H \subset G$ is a normal subgroup.

	We define the category of \emph{genuine equivariant chain complexes} as 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}} ^G := \operatorname{Mod}_{R[\mathcal{O}_G]}
	\end{align*}
	in the sense of (\cite{explicit}, Definition 2.1); that is, finite-product-preserving functors $(R[\mathcal{O}_G])^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{Sp}$.
<!-- end defi-24 -->
<!-- rem-20: body_md -->
The $t$-structure on spectra induces a $t$-structure on $\operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}}^G$. Since $R[\mathcal{O}_G]$ is additive, we can identify
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}, \geq 0} ^G \simeq \mathcal{P}_\Sigma (R[\mathcal{O}_G])
	\end{align*}
	(\cite{Gepner_2015}, Corollary 2.10).
<!-- end rem-20 -->
<!-- rem-21: body_md -->
We have deliberately avoided using Mackey functors since this will not be necessary for our purposes. More classically, one would use Mackey functors to define genuine equivariant $G$-spectra (\cite{barwick_spectra}, \cite{Guillou}), and define genuine equivariant chain complexes as the $R$-module objects in this category. However, this simplifies to the above definition (\cite{explicit}, Example 2.15).
<!-- end rem-21 -->
<!-- defi-25: body_md -->
\label{defi-strict}
	There is a limit and colimit preserving functor $\operatorname{triv}_G: \operatorname{Mod}_R \to \operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}}^G$, given by sending a chain complex to the same underlying chain complex with trivial $G$-action. This admits a right and a left adjoint, respectively written as
	\begin{align*}
		(-)^G : \operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}}^G \to \operatorname{Mod}_R, \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \;  (-)_G: \operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}}^G \to \operatorname{Mod}_R
	\end{align*}
	which we will call \emph{strict fixed points} and \emph{strict orbits}.
<!-- end defi-25 -->
<!-- rem-22: body_md -->
On objects of the form $R[G/H]$, we have that
	\begin{align*}
		R[G/H]^G \simeq R[G/H]_G \simeq R
	\end{align*}
<!-- end rem-22 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
\label{example-strictquotient}
	Let $S$ be a simplicial $G$-set. We will write $R[S]$ for the resulting genuine equivariant chain complex. That is, each simplicial level of the simplicial $R[G]$-modules $R[S]$ can be written as $R[S_i]$, where $S_i$ is a $G$-set. Then, $R[S]$, as an object in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\underline{R}}^G$, can be abstractly defined as the geometric realisation of the $R[S_i]$.

	Then, since strict orbits commute with colimits, we see that
	\begin{align*}
		R[S]_G \simeq R[S/G]
	\end{align*}
	where $S/G$ is the $1$-categorical simplicial quotient. We will also often write $\tilde{C} _*(S, R) := R[S]$, since the underlying chain complex is precisely the $R$-valued chains on the geometric realisation of $S$.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
Consider the functor $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R : \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0} \to \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$. Previously, we defined it as the sifted-colimit preserving functor of $V \mapsto V^{\otimes n}_{\Sigma_n}$ for $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_R^\omega$. Considering $V^{\otimes n}_{\Sigma_n}$ as a genuine $\Sigma_n$-chain complex, we see that this functor can always be written as $V \mapsto V^{\otimes n}_{\Sigma_n}$.
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- defi-26: body_md -->
For $n > 0$ and $i \geq 0$, we will say that a chain $\hat{0} = \sigma _0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_j = \hat{1}$ of partitions of $[n]$ has \emph{type $\leq i$} if in each of the refinements $\sigma_k \leq \sigma_{k+1}$, each part of $\sigma_{k+1}$ is refined into at most $i$ parts.
<!-- end defi-26 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop-cotsym}
	Let $m \leq n$. For $i > 0$, define the simplicial set $T_{\leq n} (m,i)$ by
	\begin{align*}
		T_{\leq n}  (m,i)_j := \left\{ \sigma_0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_j = \hat{1} \ \middle\vert \begin{array}{l} \sigma_k \text{ is a partition of } [i] \text{, the chain has type } \leq n \\ \text{and each part of } \sigma_0 \text{ has size } \leq m \end{array}  \right\} \bigsqcup \{*\}
	\end{align*}
	The face maps delete partitions from the chain, sending invalid chains to the basepoint. Degeneracy maps insert repeated partitions.

	Then, for $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$,
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq m} (V \to V)) \simeq \bigoplus_{i > 0} \left(V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq n} (m,i), R)\right) _{\Sigma_i}
	\end{align*}
	where $(-)_{\Sigma_i}$ refers to strict orbits.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- rem-23: body_md -->
Notice that for $n = \infty$ and $m = 1$, we get $\cot (\operatorname{sqz} (V))$ and we recover (\cite{partition}, Proposition 5.35).
<!-- end rem-23 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Given $(A \twoheadrightarrow R) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, we can write it as its bar resolution in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /R}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ as a $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n}$-algebra (\cref{prop-nonunital}). This means that we can write $(A \twoheadrightarrow R)$ as a geometric realisation of objects of the form $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq n}_R (V \to V) = (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V) \xrightarrow{V \mapsto 0} R)$. Notice that this is not the same as its bar resolution in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ as a $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n}$-algebra.

	$\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq m} (V)$ is a $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n}$-algebra by trivialising anything in degree higher than $m$. Remember that $\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V)) \simeq (0 \to V)$. Hence, omitting the zero (since $L_{R/R} \simeq 0$), we get
	\begin{align*}
