		\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq m}_R (V)) & \simeq | \operatorname{Bar}_\bullet (\operatorname{id}, \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq n}_R, \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq m}_R (V)) | \\
													 & \simeq \bigg|  \ \ \ldots \ \ \substack{\longrightarrow \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow   \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow   \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow} \ \ \bigoplus_{c \leq n} (\bigoplus_{b \leq n}   ( \bigoplus_{a\leq m}  V^{\otimes a}_{\Sigma_a} )^{\otimes b}_{\Sigma_b})^{\otimes c}_{ \Sigma_c}\ \ \substack{\longrightarrow \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow   \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow} \ \ \bigoplus_{b \leq n} (\bigoplus_{a \leq m}  V^{\otimes a}_{\Sigma_a})^{\otimes b}_{ \Sigma_b} \ \ \substack{  \longrightarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow} \ \ \bigoplus_{a \leq m} V^{\otimes a}_{ \Sigma_{a}} \ \ \bigg|\
	\end{align*}
	We can now apply a well-known combinatorial observation (c.f. \cite{Ching}, \S 7) and expand these exponents binomially. We see that an exponent adding up to $i$ at the $j$th simplicial level of this diagram is equivalent to a chain $\sigma_0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_j = \hat{1}$ of partitions of $[i]$. Additionally, each part of $\sigma_0$ has size $\leq n$, since the most refined part of this partition corresponds to the exponents coming from $\bigoplus_{a \leq m} V^{\otimes a}_{\Sigma_a}$. Additionally, due to the bounds on the other sums, this chain has type $\leq n$. Hence,
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\operatorname{nu}, \leq m} (V)) & \simeq  \bigg|  \ \ \ldots \ \ \substack{\longrightarrow \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow   \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow} \ \ \bigoplus_{i > 0}  (V^{\otimes i} \otimes R[T_{\leq n} (m,i)_1] )_{\Sigma_i} \ \ \substack{  \longrightarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \\ \leftarrow  \vspace{-4pt} \ \\ \longrightarrow} \ \ \bigoplus_{i > 0} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes  R[T_{\leq n} (m,i)_0])_{ \Sigma_i} \ \ \bigg| \\
													 & \simeq \bigoplus_{i > 0} \left(V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}(T_{\leq n} (m,i),R)\right)_{ \Sigma_i}
	\end{align*}
	where $R[T_{\leq n} (m,i)_j]$ refers to the free $R$-module generated by the set $T_{\leq n} (m,i)_j$ quotiented by the basepoint.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lemma-cotconnectivity}
	Let $l,m,n > 0$ be fixed. Then, $(C^* (T_{\leq n} (m,i), R) \otimes_R V^{\otimes i})_{\Sigma_i}$ is $l$-connective for $i \gg 0$ for any $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$. The bounds on $i$ do not depend on $V$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
We will write $X := C^* (T_{\leq n} (m,i), R)$ to simplify notation. Let $F: \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0} \to \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$ be the functor $V \mapsto (X \otimes_R V^{\otimes i})_{\Sigma_i}$. We may only prove this for $V$ finite and free and then left Kan extend. Then, using the binomial formula, we see that if $V = R^j$ then
	\begin{align*}
		F(V) \simeq \bigoplus_{i_1 + \dots + i_j = i}  \left( \operatorname{Ind} _{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}^{\Sigma_i} X \right)_{\Sigma_i} \simeq \bigoplus_{i_1 + \dots + i_j = i} X_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}
	\end{align*}
	Thus, it suffices to show that $T_{\leq n} (m,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ is $l$-connected for $i \gg 0$.

	A \emph{partition of $[i]$ with $i_1, \dots, i_j$ repetitions} is a partition of a set with $i_1$ undistinguishable elements, $i_2$ undistinguishable elements, and so on. We can identify the set of partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1 , \dots , i_j$ repetitions with the $(\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j})$-orbits of the set of partitions of $[i]$. Notice that we can identify $T_{\leq n} (m,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ with the simplicial set whose $r$-simplices are chains $\sigma_0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_r = \hat{1}$ of partitions of $i$ with $i_1, \dots , i_j$ repetitions (plus a basepoint), where $\sigma_0$ has all parts of size $\leq m$, and the chain is of type $\leq n$ (\cref{example-strictquotient}).

	If $n < \infty$, the result is now clear because for $i$ large enough we cannot have any such chains of length $r < l$. Hence, assume $n = \infty$.

	There is a map $T_{\leq \infty} (\infty,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}} \to T_{\leq \infty} (m,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ given by collapsing invalid chains to the basepoint. Let $\tilde{T}$ be the set-theoretic fibre of this map, which is a cofibration since it is injective at every simplicial level. Hence, $\tilde{T}$ is the simplicial set whose $r$-simplices are chains $\sigma_0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_r = \hat{1}$ of partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1 , \dots, i_j$ repetitions (plus a basepoint), where $\sigma_0$ has at least one part of size $> m$. 

	In any chain of $\tilde{T}$, each partition is a coarsening of $\sigma_0$, so all of the partitions have a part with size $> m$. Hence, by \cref{prop-unreduced}, we see that $\tilde{T}$ is the unreduced suspension of the poset of proper partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1, \dots, i_j$ repetitions and one part of size $> m$.

	This poset is atomised, and the atoms are partitions with exactly one part of size $m+1$ and every other part a singleton. Let $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_k$ be $k$ such atoms, with parts $P_1, \dots, P_k$ of size $m+1$. Their join is given by the partition with one part $P_1 \cup \dots \cup P_k$ and every other part a singleton. Hence, we see that the least number of atoms that generate this poset is $\lceil \frac{i}{m+1} \rceil$. By \cref{prop-atomised}, we see that this poset is at least $(\lceil \frac{i}{m+1} \rceil -2)$-connected.

	Hence, since $\tilde{T}$ is the unreduced suspension of this poset, it is $(\lceil \frac{i}{m+1} \rceil -1)$-connected.

	By a similar argument, $T_{\leq \infty} (\infty, i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ is the unreduced suspension of the poset of partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1 , \dots, i_j$ repetitions that are not the indiscrete partition (i.e. not a single part). But this poset has an infimum, so it is contractible. 

	Additionally, $T_{\leq \infty} (m,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ is the set-theoretic quotient of the map $\tilde{T} \to T_{\leq \infty} (\infty, i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$, and thus the homotopy cofibre since the map is a cofibration. Hence, $T_{\leq \infty} (m,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_j}}$ is the suspension of $\tilde{T}$ so it is $\lceil \frac{i}{m+1} \rceil$-connected. The result follows.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- defi-27: body_md -->
We say that $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ is \emph{nilpotent} if $\mathfrak{m} := \ker (\pi_0 (A) \to \pi_0 (B))$ is nilpotent; that is, $\mathfrak{m}^n \cong 0$ for $n \gg 0$. We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{Nil}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ for the full subcategory spanned by the nilpotent surjections. For $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$, we will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{Nil}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ for the category of nilpotent arrows with target $S$.

	We say that $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is \emph{bounded} if $\pi_i \operatorname{fib} (A \to B) \cong 0$ for $i\gg 0$.

	We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ and $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ for the corresponding categories of bounded and nilpotent arrows.
<!-- end defi-27 -->
<!-- construction-11: body_md -->
\label{construction-approxcot}
	Let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ and let $m \geq n$. Then, we can consider $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ as an object in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ by the right adjoint to polynomial truncation. Hence, there is a counit map $t_{\leq n}^m (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$. Applying $\cot_{\leq n}$, we get a map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)
	\end{align*}
	The polynomial truncation maps are compatible with each other so we get a tower
	\begin{align*}
		\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \dots \to \cot_{\leq n+1} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)
	\end{align*}
	and hence a natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \varprojlim_{m \geq n} \cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)
	\end{align*}
<!-- end construction-11 -->
<!-- construction-12: body_md -->
\label{construction-cotfiltrations}
	Let $m \leq n$. For $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$, we can consider it as an object of $\operatorname{Fil}\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ through the adic filtration. Applying $\cot_{\leq n} \circ \iota_m^n$, we get a natural filtration on $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$. All of the functors we used commute with sifted colimits, so this construction commutes with sifted colimits.

	Notice that the map $\cot_{\leq n+1} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ then refines to a map of filtered modules.
<!-- end construction-12 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lemma-cotcomplete}
	Let $m \leq n$ and let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$. Then the filtration on $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is complete.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Complete objects are closed under geometric realisations (\cite{partition}, Proposition 2.11), so we may just show this for $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) = \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq m} (V \to V \oplus W)$ for $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$. By \cref{prop-cotsym}, we have an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq m} (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \bigoplus_{i > 0} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq n} (m,i) , R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	Following the filtered weights in the proof of \cref{prop-cotsym}, we see that
	\begin{align*}
		F^j \cot_{\leq n} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq m} (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \bigoplus_{i \geq j} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq n} (m,i) , R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	By \cref{lemma-cotconnectivity}, for fixed $l$, the $j$th filtered piece is $l$-connective for $j \gg 0$. This directly implies completeness by the Milnor sequence.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lemma-cotpieces}
	Let $m > 0$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $l \geq 0$. Then, there exists a $j$ such that for any $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ the composition
		\begin{align*}
			\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)/F^j \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)
		\end{align*}
		is $l$-connected for $n \gg m$. The bounds on $n$ do not depend on $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$.
	\item Let $i$ be fixed. For any $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ the map
		\begin{align*}
			\operatorname{Gr}^i \cot (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \operatorname{Gr}^i \cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow 	B)
		\end{align*}
		is an equivalence for $n \gg m$. The bounds on $n$ do not depend on $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We may just check this on compact projectives. Choose $j$ so that for all $j' > j$ and all $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$, $(V^{\otimes j'} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq \infty} (m,i), R))_{\Sigma_{j'}}$ is $l$-connective (\cref{lemma-cotconnectivity}). Thus, for $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$ and $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) = \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq m} (V \to V \oplus W)$, the above map becomes 
	\begin{align*}
		\bigoplus_{i > 0} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq \infty} (m,i), R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W) \to \bigoplus_{0 \leq i \leq j} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C} (T_{\leq n} (m,i), R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	Every term on the left summand with $i > j$ is $l$-connective by construction, so the result follows from the fact that $T_{\leq \infty} (m,i) \simeq T_{\leq n} (m,i)$ for $n \gg m$.

	For the second part, we again reduce it to the case of compact projectives. This ends up reducing to the fact that $T_{\infty} (m,i) \simeq T_{\leq n} (m,i)$ for $n \gg m$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop-cotcolim}
	Let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$. Then, the natural map
	\begin{align*}
	\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to  \varprojlim_{n \geq m} \cot_{\leq n}  (A \twoheadrightarrow B)
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence, where this limit is computed in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The filtration on $\cot_{\leq n} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is complete for all $n$ (\cref{lemma-cotcomplete}). An inverse limit of complete filtered modules is complete, so we just need to check that this is an equivalence on gradeds. This follows from \cref{lemma-cotpieces}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- defi-28: body_md -->
Let $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ and let $f: A \to B$ be a morphism in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$. It is \emph{elementary} if it fits in a pullback diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			A \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & B \arrow{d} \\
			S \arrow{r} & S \oplus M[n]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where $M \in \operatorname{Mod}_S^\heartsuit$ and $n > 0$.

	$f: A \to B$ is \emph{small} if it is a composition of elementary morphisms.

	An object $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}$ is \emph{small} if the map $A \to S$ is small.
<!-- end defi-28 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop-smallsurjections}
	An object $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ is small if and only if it is bounded and nilpotent.

	Additionally, a morphism $f: A \to B$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ is small if and only if it is a surjection in $\pi_0$.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Suppose $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ is small. Then, it is clearly bounded and nilpotent. Hence, it suffices to prove that a morphism in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ is small if and only if it is a surjection in $\pi_0$.

	Any elementary morphism is surjective on $\pi_0$, so the same is true of any small morphism.

	Let $f: A \to B$ be surjective on $\pi_0$, and let $C := \operatorname{cofib} (A \to B)$. Let $n$ be the smallest non-negative integer such that $\pi_n (C) \neq 0$. By assumption, $n > 0$. There is an $(n+1)$-connective map $C \otimes_A B \to L_{B/A}$ (\cite{HA}, Theorem 7.4.3.1 and \cite{SAG}, Proposition 25.3.5.1), and hence an $(n+1)$-connective map $C \otimes_A S \to L_{B/A} \otimes_B S$. We have the fibre sequence
	\begin{align*}
		L_{A/R} \otimes_A B \to L_{B/R} \to L_{B/A}
	\end{align*}
	We can tensor by $S$ as $B$-modules to get a fibre sequence
	\begin{align*}
		L_{A/R} \otimes_A S \to L_{B/R} \otimes_B S \to L_{B/A} \otimes_B S
	\end{align*}
	Let $D := \pi_n (L_{B/A}\otimes_B S) \cong \pi_n (C \otimes_A S)$. Notice that $D \in \operatorname{Mod}_S^\heartsuit$. We have the trivial map $A \to S \oplus D[n] $. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{A/ /S} (B, S \oplus D[n]) & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (L_{B/A} \otimes_B S, D[n]) \\
											  & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} ( \tau _{\leq n} L_{B/A} \otimes_B S, D[n]) \\
											  & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} ( \tau _{\leq n} C \otimes_A S, D[n]) \\
											  & \simeq \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (C \otimes_A S, D[n])
	\end{align*}
	The truncation map gives us a canonical choice of a map $C \otimes_A S \to D[n]$, which induces a map $B \to S \oplus D[n]$. Let $B' := B \times_{S \oplus D[n]} S$, so we have a diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			A \arrow{dr}{f'} \arrow{ddr} \arrow{drr}{f} & & \\
																 & B' \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & B \arrow{d} \\
																 & S \arrow{r} & S \oplus D[n]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	We have a map of cofibre sequences
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			A \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & A \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & 0 \arrow{d} \\
			B' \arrow{r} & B \arrow{r} & D[n]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Hence, $C' := \operatorname{cofib} (A \to B') \simeq \operatorname{fib} (C \to D[n])$. The map $A \to S$ induces a map $C \to C \otimes_A S$, and the map $C \to D[n]$ is induced by the composition of this with the truncation $C \otimes_A S \to  \tau _{\leq n} C \otimes_A S \simeq D[n]$.

	Let $\mathfrak{m} := \ker (\pi_0 (A) \to \pi_0 (S))$. Then, $\pi_n (C') \cong \mathfrak{m} D$. We can repeat this inductively to obtain a map $A \to B'^{(m)}$, where $C'^{(n)} := \operatorname{cofib} (A \to B'^{(n)}) \in \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq n}$, $\pi_n (C'^{(n)}) \cong \mathfrak{m}^m D$ and $\pi_l (C'^{(n)}) \cong \pi_l (C)$ for all other $l$. Since $A$ is nilpotent, this process must finish, and we must eventually get an $(n+1)$-connective map $A \to B'^{(m)}$. Then we can also induct on the homotopy groups of $C$ to obtain $f$ as a composition of elementary morphisms.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- construction-13: body_md -->
\label{construction-refinedPostnikov}
	Let $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{Nil}}$. Consider the map $\tau_{\leq n+1} A \to \tau_{\leq n} A$. By the proof of \cref{prop-smallsurjections}, we can refine this to a tower of the form
	\begin{align*}
		\tau_{\leq n+1} A \to \dots \to \tau_{\leq n+1}^{i} A \to \dots \to \tau_{\leq n+1} ^{1} A \to \tau_{\leq n+1}^0 A \simeq \tau_{\leq n} A
	\end{align*}
	where
	\begin{align*}
		\pi_j (\tau_{\leq n+1} ^i A ) \cong \begin{cases} \pi_j (A) \; & \text{if $j \leq n$}	 \\ \mathfrak{m}^{i-1}\pi_{n+1} (A)/\mathfrak{m}^i \; & \text{if $j = n+1$} \\ 0 \; & \text{otherwise}	\end{cases}
	\end{align*}
	where $\mathfrak{m}$ is the kernel ideal of $\pi_0 (A) \to \pi_0 (S)$. Since $\mathfrak{m}^ i = 0$ for $i \gg 0$, $\tau_{\leq n+1}^i A \simeq \tau_{\leq n+1} A$ for $i \gg 0$. Each of the steps in this tower comes from a pullback diagram of the form
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\tau_{\leq n+1} ^{i+1} A \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \tau_{\leq n+1}^i A \arrow{d} \\
			\tau_{\leq n+1}^i  A \arrow{r} & \tau_{\leq n+1}^i A \oplus \mathfrak{m}^i \pi_{n+1} (A)/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1} [n+2]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The module $\mathfrak{m}^i \pi_{n+1} (A) /\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ is a $\pi_0 (A)/\mathfrak{m} \cong \pi_0 (S)$-module.

	Additionally, the construction in \cref{prop-smallsurjections} makes this tower functorial, meaning that a map $A \to B$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{Nil}}$ induces a map between these refined towers, as well as between the square-zero extension diagrams.
<!-- end construction-13 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop-Nilimage}
	Let $S \in \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ and let $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$. Then, $A$ is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ for some $n$.

	Additionally, if $A \to B$ is a map in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, it is also in the image of $\iota_n^\infty$ for some $n$.
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By \cref{prop-smallsurjections}, any object $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ can be written as a finite pullback of trivial square-zero extensions. Also, for $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$, $S \oplus V$ is in the image of $\iota_1^\infty$ as a free algebra. Hence, since $\iota_n^\infty$ commutes with limits, for the first part it suffices to show that if $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ and $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$ is eventually coconnective, the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim_{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, S \oplus V) \to \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, S \oplus V) 
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence. Using the adjunction, it suffices to show that
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim _{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S), V) \to  \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S), V)
	\end{align*} 
	is an equivalence. We will show that this is an equivalence on homotopy groups. For $\pi_0$, we need to show that any map $\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S) \to V$ factors through $\cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S)$ for some $m$. Since $V$ is truncated, we may just show that any map $\tau_{\leq i} \cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S) \to V$ factors through $\tau_{\leq i} \cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S)$ for some $i$. This follows from \cref{lemma-cotpieces}, since the map $\tau_{\leq i} \cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S) \to \tau_{\leq i} \cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S)$ admits a section for $m \gg n$.

	Now take $l > 0$. Then, $\pi_l \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S), V)  \cong \pi_0 \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S), \tau_{\geq 0} V[-l])$ and similar for $\cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S)$. $\tau_{\geq 0} V[-l]$ is bounded so the claim follows just as in the case $l = 0$.

	For the last part, let $A,B \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$. We must show that any map $A \to B$ is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty$ for some $n$. We just proved that $A$ is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty$ for some $n$. We can again build $B$ by a sequence of square-zero extensions. If $B = S \oplus V$, where $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$ is eventually coconnective, we just proved the result, since
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, S \oplus V) \simeq \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot (A \twoheadrightarrow S), V) \simeq \varinjlim _{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_S} (\cot_{\leq m} (A \twoheadrightarrow S), V)
	\end{align*}
	so any map $A \to S \oplus V$ comes from $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ for some $m$.

	We will now induct on the square-zero extension diagrams. Write $B' = B \times_{S \oplus V} S$, where $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{S, \geq 0}$ is eventually coconnective, $B$ is in the image of $\iota_n ^\infty$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}}(A, B') \simeq \varinjlim_{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, B')$. By increasing $n$ if necessary, we may assume that the map $B \to S \oplus V$ is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty$. Since the functors $\iota_n^m$ commute with limits, $B'$ is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, B') & \simeq \operatorname{fib} \left(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, B) \to  \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}}} (A,  S \oplus V)\right) \\
		& \simeq \operatorname{fib} \left( \varinjlim _{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, B) \to \varinjlim _{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A,  S \oplus V) \right)  \\
		& \simeq \varinjlim_{m \geq n} \operatorname{fib} \left( \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, B) \to \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, S \oplus V) \right) \\
		& \simeq \varinjlim_{m \geq n} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /S}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (A, B')
	\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lemma-symncomplete}
	Let $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$. Then, there is an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		F^j \operatorname{adic} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \bigoplus_{i > 0} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (S^{\geq j} (n,i), R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	Where $S^{\geq j} (n,i)$ is the simplicial set whose $l$-simplices are given by
	\begin{align*}
		S^{\geq j} (n,i)_l := \left\{ \sigma_0 \leq \dots \leq \sigma_i \ \middle\vert \begin{array}{l} \sigma_r \text{ is a partition of } [i] \text{ with $\geq j$ parts}  \\ \text{and each part of } \sigma_0 \text{ has size } \leq n \end{array}  \right\} \bigsqcup \{*\}
	\end{align*}
	Additionally, if $n < \infty$, this filtration is complete.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Note that $F^j \operatorname{adic}(\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \bigoplus_{i \geq j} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\geq j} (V) \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)$, where $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\geq j} (V) = \bigoplus_{i \geq j} V^{\otimes i}_{\Sigma_i}$. We can use the bar construction as in \cref{prop-cotsym}, to obtain the result.

	Now we show completeness. First we will show that for fixed $j$, $l$ and $n$, $(V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (S^{\geq j} (n,i)))_{\Sigma_i}$ is $l$-connected for $i \gg 0$ for any $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{R, \geq 0}$, and the bounds on $i$ do not depend on $V$. We proceed exactly as in \cref{lemma-cotconnectivity}.

	Firstly, we just need to show that $S^{\geq j} (n,i) /_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}}$ is $l$-connected for $i \gg 0$. Let $\tilde{S}$ be the set-theoretic fibre of the map $S^{\geq j} (\infty, i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}} \to S^{\geq j} (n,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}}$ that collapses invalid chains. 

	The map $\tilde{S} \to S^{\geq j} (\infty, i) /_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}}$ is a cofibration, so we get a cofibre sequence $\tilde{S} \to S^{\geq j} (\infty, \i) /_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}} \to S^{\geq j} (n,i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}}$.

	We can identify $\tilde{S}$ with the poset of partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1, \dots, i_r$ repetitions with at least one part of size $> n$ and $\geq j$ parts (\cref{example-strictquotient}). This poset is atomised and the atoms are the partitions with exactly one part of size $(n+1)$ and the rest singletons.

	Let $\sigma_1, \dots , \sigma_t$ be $t$ such atoms, with parts $P_1, \dots, P_t$ of size $n+1$. Their join is given by the partition with one part $P_1 \cup \dots \cup P_t$ and every other part a singleton, provided that this has at least $j$ parts. Hence, the least number of atoms that generate this poset is $\lceil \frac{i-j}{n+1} \rceil$. By \cref{prop-atomised}, this simplicial set is $\lceil \left( \frac{i-j}{n+1} \rceil -2\right)$-connected.

	The simplicial set $S^{\geq j} (\infty, i)/_{\Sigma_{i_1} \times \dots \times \Sigma_{i_r}}$ is the poset of partitions of $[i]$ with $i_1, \dots, i_r$ repetitions with at least $j$ parts. But this has an infimum so it is contractible. Hence, $S^{\geq j} (n,i)$ is the suspension of $\tilde{S}$ and it is $\left( \lceil \frac{i-j}{n+1} \rceil \right)$-connected, and this quantity gets arbitrarily large.

	In particular, this shows that	
	\begin{align*}
		F^j \operatorname{adic} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W)) \simeq \prod_{i > 0} (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (S^{\geq j} (n,i), R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	This allows us to write $\operatorname{adic} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W))$ as a product of filtered modules $A_i$ where
	\begin{align*}
		F^j A_i \simeq (V^{\otimes i} \otimes \tilde{C}_* (S^{\geq j} (n,i), R))_{\Sigma_i} \otimes_R \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* (W)
	\end{align*}
	We may just show that this is complete, but this is clear because there are no partitions of $i$ with at least $j$ parts for $j > i$, so $S^{\geq j} (n,i) \simeq *$ for $j > i$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
Let $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ be a map in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$ that is $\pi_0$-surjective such that the kernel ideal of $\pi_0 (A)$ is nilpotent. Then, $\operatorname{adic} (A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ is complete.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Note that if $(A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to (C \twoheadrightarrow D)$ is $n$-connected, so is $\operatorname{adic} (A \twoheadrightarrow B) \to \operatorname{adic} (C \twoheadrightarrow D)$. By the Milnor sequence, it is enough then to show that $\operatorname{adic} (\tau_{\leq i} A \twoheadrightarrow \tau_{\leq i} B)$ is complete for all $i$, so we may assume that both $A$ and $B$ are eventually coconnective.

	The map between truncations is nilpotent and bounded, so it is in the image of $\iota_n^\infty : \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ for some $n$ (\cref{prop-Nilimage}). The functor $\iota_n^\infty$ commutes with sifted colimits, so using the bar resolution in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, we can write $(A \twoheadrightarrow B)$ as a geometric realisations of objects of the form $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W)$, where $V,W \in \operatorname{Vect}_R$.

	We are now done because complete objects are closed under geometric realisations and $\operatorname{adic} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^{\leq n} (V \to V \oplus W))$ is complete (\cref{lemma-symncomplete}).
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
Let $n < \infty$. Then, the adjunction
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n}^\vee : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee[1]}^{\text{op}}: \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)
	\end{align*}
	is comonadic.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
This follows exactly the same proof as \cref{prop-cotcomonadic}, but we can't just dualise that result because duality might not take totalisations to geometric realisations. 

	Since duality gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0} \simeq (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})^{\text{op}}$, we see that $X^\bullet$ is $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee$-split. Since $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee (\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) \simeq \cot_{\leq n}^\vee (X^\bullet)(1)$, we get an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		| \cot_{\leq n}^\vee (\operatorname{Gr}	\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) | \xrightarrow{\simeq} \cot_{\leq n}^\vee (\operatorname{Tot} (\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)))
	\end{align*}
	Then, the map
	\begin{align*}
		| \cot_{\leq n} ^\vee (\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)) | \xrightarrow{\simeq} \cot_{\leq n}^\vee (\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (X^\bullet)))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence on gradeds, so it is an equivalence. The result follows from applying $\operatorname{aug}$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lemma-truecotcolim}
	If $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$, there is a natural equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim_{n \geq m} \cot_{\leq n}^\vee (A) \simeq \cot^\vee (A)
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
There is a natural filtration on $\cot_{\leq m}^\vee (A)$ that is complete (\cref{lemma-cotcomplete}). Dualising, we get an increasing filtration that	is cocomplete, meaning that the filtered colimit of the filtered pieces vanishes. Thus, it suffices to check an equivalence on gradeds. This is true by dualising \cref{lemma-cotpieces}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- defi-29: body_md -->
We will say that a tower $X_0 \to \dots \to  X_i \to \dots$ in $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$ is \emph{almost eventually constant} if for each $j$, the map $\tau_{\geq j} X_n\to \tau_{\geq j} X_{n+1}$ is an equivalence for $n \gg 0$.

	Let $F: \operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a functor where $\mathcal{C}$ is an $\infty$-category with sifted colimits. $F$ is \emph{regular} if it preserves almost eventually constant towers.

	We will say that $F$ preserves \emph{finite stable geometric realisations} if it preserves colimits of diagrams $\Delta^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$ that are left Kan extended from $(\Delta^{\leq n})^{\text{op}}$ for some $n$ such that the geometric realisation, when computed in $\operatorname{Solid}_k$, is in $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$.
<!-- end defi-29 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lemma-completion}
	Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $\infty$-category that admits sifted colimits. Then, restriction gives an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fun} _{\Sigma} (\operatorname{Solid}_k, \mathcal{C}) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Fun}_{\sigma}' (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}, \mathcal{C})
	\end{align*}
	where $\operatorname{Fun}_{\Sigma} ( \operatorname{Solid}_k, \mathcal{C}) \subset \operatorname{Fun} (\operatorname{Solid}_k, \mathcal{C}) $ refers to the full subcategory of sifted-colimit-preserving functors, and $\operatorname{Fun}_{\sigma}' (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}, \mathcal{C}) \subset \operatorname{Fun} (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}, \mathcal{C})$ refers to the full subcategory of regular functors that preserve finite stable geometric realisations.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. Notice that since $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$ is closed under colimits, it suffices to show the above result for $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$. By (\cite{explicit}, Proposition 2.39), it suffices to show that $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$ is equivalent to its category of pro-coherent modules and that its dually almost perfect modules are equivalent to $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}, \kappa}$.

	In the language of (\cite{explicit}, \S 2), $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$ can be identified with the category of modules over the small category $\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)_{< \kappa}$. The opposite of this category is just the category of vector spaces of dimension $< \kappa$. Notice that every object is projective, so it is clear that almost perfect objects in the stable $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)_{< \kappa}^{\text{op}}}$ are equivalent to the category of bounded below chain complexes of vector spaces of dimension $< \kappa$. Hence, the coherent ones are precisely the bounded chain complexes of dimension $< \kappa$, which are dually equivalent to the bounded chain complexes in $\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)_{< \kappa}$. By (\cite{ultrasolid}, Proposition 2.25), we see that pro-coherent modules in $\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)_{< \kappa}$ are just $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$.

	From this one easily deduces that the dually almost perfect objects are precisely $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}} \cap \operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
The monad $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee \circ \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)$ on $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ admits a unique extension to a sifted-colimit-preserving monad on $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
This follows by exactly the same proof as (\cite{foliations}, Proposition 3.8). By (\cite{explicit}, Proposition 4.20), we just need to show that $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee \circ \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)$ preserves the following kind of colimits in $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Towers  $M_1 \to M_2 \to \dots$  such that for all $i$, the tower $\pi_i (M_1) \to \pi_i (M_2) \to \dots$ is eventually constant.
		\item Simplicial diagrams $X^\bullet$ in $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$ that are left Kan extended from $(\Delta^{\leq m})^{\text{op}}$ for some $m$, such that $|X^\bullet|$, when computed in $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, is in $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.
	\end{enumerate}
	The first part is clear because if $A \to B$ is a map in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$ that is $i$-connective, then $\cot (A) \to \cot(B)$ is $i$-connective.

	For the second one, we will use the filtrations on $\cot$ from \cref{construction-cotfiltrations}. That is, $\operatorname{sqz} ((X^\vee)^\bullet)$ factors through the category $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R / /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq 1}$, and this gives us a complete filtration on $\cot \circ \operatorname{sqz} ((X^\vee)^\bullet)$. Dualising, we get an increasing filtration that is \emph{cocomplete}; that is, the colimit of the filtered pieces vanishes. Equivalences are detected on gradeds, and filtered colimits of cocomplete increasingly filtered objects are closed under geometric realisations, so it suffices to show the equivalence after taking gradeds.

	Given a derivation $\alpha: L_{k/R}[-1] \to V$, the filtration on $\cot \circ \operatorname{sqz} (V)$ is obtained by putting $V$ in filtered degree $1$ and $L_{k/R}[-1]$ in filtered degree $0$. The associated graded is the trivial derivation, so we may assume that all of the derivations are trivial.

	In this case, we use \cref{prop-cotsym}, since $\operatorname{sqz} (L_{k/R}[-1] \xrightarrow{0} V) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq 1} (V \to V)$. We just need to show that the functor $F: \operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}} \to \operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		V \mapsto (V^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C}^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1, n), k))^{\Sigma_n}
	\end{align*}
	preserves the relevant colimits. Let $X^\bullet$ be a simplicial diagram in $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$ that is left Kan extended from $(\Delta^{\leq m})^{\text{op}}$ such that the geometric realisation, when computed in $\operatorname{Solid}_k$, is in $\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$. Then, tensoring with itself $n$ times gives an $n$-simplicial diagram, to which the diagonal is cofinal. We will write $(X^\bullet)^{\otimes n}$ for the diagonal simplicial diagram, which is left Kan extended from $(\Delta^{\leq mn})^{\text{op}}$ (\cite{polynomialfunctors}, Proposition 2.10). Since we are in a stable category, finite colimits commute with limits, and $(V^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C}^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1,n), k))^{\Sigma_n}$ is left Kan extended from $(\Delta^{\leq nm})^{\text{op}}$. Then, using that finite colimits commute with limits in $\operatorname{Solid}_k$,
	\begin{align*}
		|((X^\bullet)^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C}^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1, n), k))^{\Sigma_n}|  & \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_{(\Delta^{\leq mn})^{\text{op}}} ((X^\bullet)^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C} ^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1,n), k))^{\Sigma_n} \\
		& \simeq  (( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_{(\Delta^{\leq mn})^{\text{op}}} X^\bullet)^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C} ^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1,n), k))^{\Sigma_n} \\
		& \simeq (|X^\bullet|^{\otimes n} \otimes \tilde{C}^* (T_{\leq \infty} (1,n), k))^{\Sigma_n}
	\end{align*}
	as required.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- defi-30: body_md -->
Let $n > 0$. The \emph{dually $n$-truncated partition Lie algebroid monad}, written as $\operatorname{Lie}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}_{\Delta, k/R}$, is the unique sifted-colimit-preserving extension of the monad $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee \circ \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)$ on $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.

	We will write
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}_{\Delta, k/R} := \operatorname{Alg}_{\operatorname{Lie}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}_{\Delta, k/R}} ((\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee[1]})
	\end{align*}
	for the $\infty$-category of algebras over this monad.

	For $n = \infty$, we will write $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi} := \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} \infty}$ for the \emph{partition Lie algebroid monad} and $\operatorname{LieAlgd}^{\pi, \blacksquare}_{\Delta, k/R} := \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} \infty, \blacksquare}$ for its category of algebras.
<!-- end defi-30 -->
<!-- rem-24: body_md -->
For $m \leq n$, we have a factorisation of the $\cot_{\leq n}^\vee$ and $\operatorname{sqz}(-^\vee)$ adjunction
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{r}{t_{\leq m}^n} \arrow{dr}{\cot_{\leq n}^\vee} & \operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \arrow{d}{\cot_{\leq m}^\vee} \\
																												 & \left( (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee[1]}\right) ^{\text{op}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The counit map on the comonad $t_{\leq m}^n \circ \iota_m^n \to \operatorname{id}$ induces a map of monads $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$ (\cite{explicit}, Lemma 3.10). Hence, we get a tower of monads
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R} ^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n+1}\to \dots  \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi} 
	\end{align*}
	Thus, for $m < n$, we have a right adjoint $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare}$ that is the identity on the underlying chain complex. Informally, any $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$-algebra has the canonical structure of a $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebra. We will often abuse notation, and for $\mathfrak{g} \in \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}$, we will still write $\mathfrak{g}$ for its image in $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare}$.
<!-- end rem-24 -->
<!-- construction-14: body_md -->
The adjunction gives us functors
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}}
	\end{align*}
	This admits a right adjoint
	\begin{align*}
		C^*_{\leq n} : \left( \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} \right) ^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}
	\end{align*}
	By \cref{lemma-squarecommutes}, for $m < n$ the left adjoints fit in a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{d}{ t _{\leq m}^{n}} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n }} & (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}} \arrow{d} \\
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m}} & (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	We will write $\mathfrak{D} := \mathfrak{D}^{\leq \infty}$ for the Koszul duality functor $\mathfrak{D}: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} \to (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi})^{\text{op}}$.
<!-- end construction-14 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lemma-squarecommutes}
	Let $m \leq n$. Then, the diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{d}{ t _{\leq m}^{n}} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n }} & (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}} \arrow{d} \\
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m}} & (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	is commutative.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
We will prove it abstractly. Let $F: \mathcal{C} \leftrightarrows \mathcal{D} : G$ be an adjunction between $\infty$-categories with an initial or final object. By (\cite{explicit}, Lemma 3.10), the functor $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{D}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathcal{C})$ given by $T \mapsto GTF$ is lax monoidal. Additionally, we can identify $\mathcal{C}$ as a full subcategory of $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{C})$ given by the constant functor (here we are using the existence of an initial or final object, so that these constant functors are given by left/right Kan extension from the initial/final object). We will abuse notation and write $\operatorname{LMod} (\mathcal{C})$ for the category of modules in $\mathcal{C}$ over $\operatorname{End} (\mathcal{C})$. That is, objects in $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{C})$ consist of pairs $(T,M)$ where $T$ is a monad in $\mathcal{C}$ and $M$ is a $T$-algebra. A map $(T,M) \to (T',M')$ is given by a map of monads $T \to T'$ and a map of $T$-algebras $M \to M'$. Define $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D})$ similarly.

	This fits in a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D}) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{C}) \arrow{d} \\
			\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{D}) \arrow{r} & \operatorname{End}(\mathcal{C})
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where the arrow $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathcal{D})$ is the biCartesian fibration classifying $T \mapsto \operatorname{Alg}_T (\mathcal{D})$, and similar for $\mathcal{C}$. Informally, for an object $(T,M)$ in $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D})$, the object $GM$ has the structure of a $GTF$-algebra. Clearly, the map $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D}) \to \operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{C})$ preserves Cartesian edges: the Cartesian edges are those $(T,M) \to (T',M')$ such that the map $M \to M'$ of $T$-algebras is an equivalence, and these are preserved due to the map $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{D}) \to \operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal{C})$ being compatible with the forgetful functors to $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{C}$.

	Consider the above situation for $\mathcal{C} = (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m})^{\text{op}}$, $\mathcal{D} = (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, $F = \operatorname{sqz}(-)^\vee$ and $G = \cot^\vee_{\leq n}$. Then, the functor $ t_{\leq m} ^n \circ \iota_m^n$ is a comonad and has a counit map $\iota_m^n \circ t_{\leq m}^n \to \operatorname{id}$. Since in the above diagram Cartesian edges are preserved, we get a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{coAlg}_{ t_{\leq m} ^n \circ \iota_m^n } (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} )^{\text{op}}\arrow{d} \\
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}  \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m}} &  (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Notice that there is a factorisation
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{r} \arrow{dr}{t^n_{\leq m}} & \operatorname{coAlg}_{ t_{\leq m}^n \circ \iota_m^n} (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}) \arrow{d} \\
			& \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	(\cite{HA}, Proposition 4.7.3.3). So it suffices to show that the functor $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare})^{\text{op}}$ factorises through $\left( \operatorname{coAlg}_{ t_{\leq m}^n \circ \iota_m^n} (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}) \right) ^{\text{op}}$. We will prove this abstractly.

	Let $\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{E}$ be $\infty$-categories with a final or initial object so that we can consider them as full subcategories of their endomorphism categories as constant functors. Consider adjunctions $F_1: \mathcal{C} \leftrightarrows \mathcal{D} : G_1$ and $F_2: \mathcal{D} \leftrightarrows \mathcal{E}: G_2$, and let $F = F_2 \circ F_1$, $G = G_1 \circ G_2$. As before, we have lax monoidal functors $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{E}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathcal{D}) \to \operatorname{End}(\mathcal{C})$.

	This induces natural functors $\operatorname{LMod}(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{E})) \to \operatorname{LMod}(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{D})) \to \operatorname{LMod}(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{C}))$. The natural map $\mathcal{E} \to \operatorname{Alg}_{G \circ F} (\mathcal{C})$ can be described by the restriction of this composition to the full subcategory of $\operatorname{LMod}(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal{E}))$ spanned by pairs $(\operatorname{id}, X)$, where $X$ is a constant functor. This trivially gives a factorisation 
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathcal{E} \arrow{r} \arrow{dr} \arrow{r} & \operatorname{Alg}_{G_2 \circ F_2} (\mathcal{D}) \arrow{d} \\
															 & \operatorname{Alg}_{G \circ F} (\mathcal{C})
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The result now follows from letting $\mathcal{C} = (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, $\mathcal{D} = \left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \right) ^{\text{op}}$, $\mathcal{E} = \left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right)^{\text{op}}$, $(F_1, G_1) = (\operatorname{sqz}(-^\vee), \cot_{\leq m}^\vee)$ and $(F_2, G_2) = (\iota_m^n, t_{\leq m}^n)$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- rem-25: body_md -->
\label{rem-KDcolim}
	The previous commutative diagram refines \cref{construction-approxcot} to a map of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebras. That is, if $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$ and $m \leq  n$, applying $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m}$ to the counit map $ t _{\leq m}^n  A \to A$, gives a natural map of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebras
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D} ^{\leq m} (A) \to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A)	
	\end{align*}
	where we are considering $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}(A)$ as a $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebra.

	By \cref{prop-cotcolim}, these maps assemble into an equivalence of chain complexes
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim _{m \leq n} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D} (A)
	\end{align*}
<!-- end rem-25 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop-Lievalues}
	Let $V \in \operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}}$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} (  V \xrightarrow{0} L_{k/R}^\vee [1] ) \simeq \left( \left(  \bigoplus_{i \geq 0}  \left( \tilde{C}_* (T_{\leq n}(1,i), k)  \otimes (V^\vee) ^{\otimes i}\right)  _{\Sigma_i} \right)^\vee \xrightarrow{0} L_{k/R}^\vee [1] \right) 
	\end{align*}
	where the subscript $\Sigma_i$ refers to strict orbits (\cref{defi-strict}).
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{prop-Liecolim}
	There is an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi} \simeq \varinjlim_n \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}
	\end{align*}
	where the colimit is taken in the category of monads on $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Firstly, notice that since all the monads involved commute with filtered colimits, the colimit is computed pointwise. All of the monads commute with sifted colimits, so it is enough to check on $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$. 

	For $V \in (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$, $\operatorname{sqz} (V^\vee)$ is in the image of $\iota_1^\infty$. The result follows by \cref{lemma-truecotcolim}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm-Liecolim}
	There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare} \simeq \varprojlim _n \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}
	\end{align*}
	where the transition maps $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n+1, \blacksquare} \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}$ are the right adjoints induced by the maps of monads $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n+1}$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare} \left( (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} \right)  \simeq \left( \varprojlim \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right)^{\text{op}}
	\end{align*}
	where the transition maps $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n+1} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ are polynomial truncation.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
For $n < \infty$, the adjunction
	\begin{align*}
		\cot^\vee : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \leftrightarrows (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})^{\text{op}}_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} : \operatorname{sqz} (-^\vee)
	\end{align*}
	is comonadic (\cref{prop-cotcomonadic}). Additionally, there is a commutative square
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n+1} \arrow{d}{ t _{\leq n}^{n+1}} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n+1 }} & \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n+1, \blacksquare} \left( (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} \right)   \arrow{d} \\
				\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \arrow{r}{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}} & \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} \left( (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} \right) 
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	(\cref{lemma-squarecommutes}). The horizontal arrows are equivalences, and combining this with \cref{thm-Liecolim} we get the desired result.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- construction-15: body_md -->
\label{construction-smallKD}
	Let $\sigma$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. For $\sigma$ large enough, the monad $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$ preserves the full subcategory $(\operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}  \subset (\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$. We will write $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} \subset \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare}$ for the full subcategory of dually truncated partition Lie algebroids whose underlying chain complex is $\sigma$-ultrasolid. This subcategory is closed under all colimits. The inclusion admits a right adjoint $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma}$. We will write
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}_\sigma : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \to \left( \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} \right) ^{\text{op}}
	\end{align*}
	for the composition of $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}$ with this right (left in the opposite category) adjoint.

	This admits a right adjoint
	\begin{align*}
		C^*_{\leq n, \sigma} : \left( \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} \right)^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end construction-15 -->
<!-- defi-31: body_md -->
Let $\sigma$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. We will say that $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_k$ is \emph{$\sigma$-small} if $\pi_i (V)$ has dimension $< \sigma$ for all $i$.

	We will write $\left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right)^\sigma \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ for the full subcategory consisting of $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ such that $\cot(A)$ is $\sigma$-small.
<!-- end defi-31 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lemma-smallKD}
	Let $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ be uncountable strong limit cardinals with $ \sigma < \sigma'$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}_\sigma |_{ \left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right) ^\sigma} \simeq \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n}_{\sigma'} | _{\left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right)^\sigma}
	\end{align*}
	Additionally,
	\begin{align*}
		C^* _{\leq n, \sigma'} |_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} } \simeq C^* _{\leq n , \sigma}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
If $A \in \left( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n} \right) ^\sigma$, the dual of $\cot(A)$, computed in $\operatorname{Solid}_k$, is in $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma \subset \operatorname{Solid}_k$. Hence, $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \in \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} \subset \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$.

	The result now follows from the fact that the left adjoint
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma} \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare, \sigma'}
	\end{align*}
	is fully faithful, so the unit is an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\label{prop-truncatedpushout}
	Let $n < \infty$ and let $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ be maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ that are surjective on $\pi_0$. Then, the natural map of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$-algebras
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence.
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Firstly, note that if $U,V,W \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$ and we have $\pi_0$-surjective maps $U \to W$, $V \to W$ in $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$, the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz} (U)) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(W))} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(V)) \to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(U) \times_{\operatorname{sqz} (W)} \operatorname{sqz} (V)) \simeq \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(U \times_W V))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence. Indeed, $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(U)), \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(V))$ and $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (\operatorname{sqz}(W))$ are the free $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$-algebras on $U^\vee, V^\vee$ and $W^\vee$ respectively. Similarly, the right hand side is the free $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$-algebra on $U^\vee \sqcup_{W^\vee} V^\vee$. Hence, this equivalence amounts to the fact that the free algebra functor commutes with colimits.

	We will use the comonadicity from \cref{prop-cotcomonadic}. Let $A^\bullet$, $B^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$ be the bar resolutions of $A, B$ and $C$ respectively, so that $A^i := (\operatorname{sqz} \circ \cot_{\leq n})^{\circ (i+1)} (A)$ and similar for $B$ and $C$. Let $X^\bullet := A^\bullet \times_{C^\bullet} B^\bullet$, so that $A \times_C B \simeq \operatorname{Tot} (X^\bullet)$.

	By our discussion of the free case, we have that the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A^i) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C^i)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B^i) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (X^i)
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence.

	Then, $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \simeq | \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A^\bullet) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C^\bullet)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B^\bullet)| \simeq |\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (X^\bullet)|$. Hence, it suffices to show that $|\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (X^\bullet)| \simeq \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)$.

	For this, consider the cosimplicial object $\tilde{X}^\bullet := \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (A^\bullet) \times_{\operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (C^\bullet)} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (B^\bullet)$ in $\operatorname{Fil} \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$, so that $\operatorname{aug}( \tilde{X}^\bullet )\simeq X^\bullet$. By construction, $\cot_{\leq n} (A^\bullet)$, $\cot_{\leq n} (B^\bullet)$ and $\cot_{\leq n} (C^\bullet)$ are all split. Additionally, $\operatorname{Gr} \operatorname{adic}_{\leq n} (-) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n}  (\cot_{\leq n} (-)(1))$, so 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Gr} (\tilde{X}^\bullet) \simeq \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n} (\cot_{\leq n} (A^\bullet)(1)) \times_{\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n} (\cot_{\leq n} (C^\bullet)(1))} \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\operatorname{Gr}, \leq n}  (\cot_{\leq n} (B^\bullet)(1))
	\end{align*}
	We can take fibre products to turn the splittings on $\cot_{\leq n} (A^\bullet)$, $\cot_{\leq n} (B^\bullet)$ and $\cot_{\leq n} (C^\bullet)$ into a splitting of $\operatorname{Gr}(\tilde{X}^\bullet)$. This implies that the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n}(\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Gr}(\tilde{X}^\bullet))) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Tot}(\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Gr}(\tilde{X}^\bullet)))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence. Lifting to filtered objects, since everything is complete, implies that the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\cot_{\leq n} (\operatorname{Tot} (\tilde{X}^\bullet)) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Tot} (\cot_{\leq n} (\tilde{X}^\bullet))
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence. Applying the functor $\operatorname{aug}$, we get the result.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- construction-16: body_md -->
\label{construction-pushoutdiagram}
	Let $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ be maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$. For $m \leq n$, the natural transformation $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (-) \to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (-)$ from \cref{rem-KDcolim} gives a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathfrak{D} ^{\leq m} (A) \bigsqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (B) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (A \times_C B) \arrow{d} \\
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \bigsqcup ^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where the superscript $\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m$ in the coproduct symbol means that the colimit is taken in the category of $\operatorname{Alg}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebras.

	The map $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \bigsqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B)\to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)$ is induced by the diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C) \arrow{d} \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \arrow{d} \\
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	in the category of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebras. Note that this diagram lifts to $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}$-algebras as follows
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C) \arrow{d} \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \arrow{d} \arrow{ddr} & \\
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \arrow{r} \arrow{drr} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \bigsqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)}^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B)\arrow{dr} & \\
												& & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	This implies that there is a factorisation
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n}_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \to \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
	\end{align*}
	So we obtain the following variation on the first commutative diagram.
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathfrak{D} ^{\leq m} (A) \bigsqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (B) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (A \times_C B) \arrow{d} \\
			\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \bigsqcup ^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Notice that this is also valid for $n = \infty$.
<!-- end construction-16 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{prop-pushoutascolimit}
	Let $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ be maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$. Then, the natural map of chain complexes
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim_{n \geq m} \; \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} ^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D} (A) \sqcup _{\mathfrak{D}(C)} \mathfrak{D}(B)
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence.
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Remember that by the bar resolution we can write
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \simeq | (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet + 1)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A))|
	\end{align*}
	and similar for $\mathfrak{D} (A)$. The map $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \to \mathfrak{D}(A)$ can be written simplicially. We have a map 
	\begin{align*}
		(\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet + 1)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A)) \to (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi)^{\circ (\bullet + 1)} (\mathfrak{D}(A))
	\end{align*}
	given by the composition of the map $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \to \mathfrak{D} (A)$ and the map of monads $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi}$. Similarly for $B$ and $C$. Taking the pushout of these simplicial diagrams, we see that
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \simeq \big\lvert \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \left(  (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet )} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A)) \sqcup_{(\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C))}^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} 1} (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B)) \right) \big\rvert
	\end{align*}
	where the superscript $\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} 1$ in the pushout means we are taking the pushout as chain complexes over $L_{k/R}^\vee [1]$.

	We have the same resolution for $\mathfrak{D}(A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D} (C)} \mathfrak{D}(B)$ by setting $n = \infty$. Once again, the map between these pushouts can be written simplicially. That is, we have a map
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \left(  (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet )} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A)) \sqcup_{(\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C))}^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} 1} (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n})^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B)) \right) \\
		\to  \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi \left(  (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi)^{\circ (\bullet )} (\mathfrak{D} (A)) \sqcup_{(\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi)^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D} (C))}^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} 1} (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi)^{\circ (\bullet)} (\mathfrak{D} (B)) \right)
	\end{align*}
	which is induced by the maps $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \to \mathfrak{D}(A)$, $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B)\to \mathfrak{D} (B)$, $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C) \to \mathfrak{D} (C)$, and the map of monads $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \to \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi}$.

	Since colimits commute with colimits, it suffices to check that the map at each simplicial level is an equivalence after taking filtered colimits. But this is true because the natural map $\varinjlim_n \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D}(A)$ is an equivalence (\cref{rem-KDcolim}), similarly for $B$ and $C$, $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi \simeq \varinjlim_n \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} $ (\cref{prop-Liecolim}), and all of these monads commute with filtered colimits.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- prop-20: body_md -->
\label{prop-KDpushout}
	Let $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ be maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ that are surjective on $\pi_0$. Then, the natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}(A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}(C)} \mathfrak{D}(B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D}(A \times_C B)
	\end{align*}
	is an equivalence.
<!-- end prop-20 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Notice that it is enough to check that this is an equivalence at the level of chain complexes.

	By \cref{prop-Nilimage}, we may choose $m$ large enough so that the maps $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ lift to $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}$. By \cref{construction-pushoutdiagram}, for any $n \geq m$ we have a commutative diagram
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathfrak{D} ^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B) \arrow{d} \\
			\mathfrak{D}(A) \sqcup _{\mathfrak{D} (C)} \mathfrak{D} (B) \arrow{r} & \mathfrak{D} (A \times_C B)
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	and these maps are compatible with each other as $n$ varies. By \cref{prop-pushoutascolimit}, the left vertical maps assemble into an equivalence 
	\begin{align*}
		\varinjlim_{n \geq m} \; \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup_{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} ^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D} (A) \sqcup _{\mathfrak{D}(C)} \mathfrak{D}(B)
	\end{align*}
	and by \cref{rem-KDcolim}, the right vertical maps assemble into an equivalence $\varinjlim_{n \geq m} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{D}(A \times_C B)$. Hence, the map $\mathfrak{D}(A) \sqcup _{\mathfrak{D} (C)} \mathfrak{D} (B) \to \mathfrak{D} (A \times_C B)$ can be written as a filtered colimit of the maps $\mathfrak{D} ^{\leq n} (A) \sqcup^{\operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} _{\mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (C)} \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (B) \to  \mathfrak{D}^{\leq n} (A \times_C B)$. But each of these maps is an equivalence by \cref{prop-truncatedpushout}, so we are done.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop-KDfullyfaithful}
	The functor
	\begin{align*}
		\mathfrak{D}: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \left( \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare} \right)  ^{\text{op}}
	\end{align*}
	is fully faithful and for any $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, the unit map $A \to C^* ( \mathfrak{D} (A))$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
It suffices to show that the unit map is an equivalence, since then the functor being fully faithful follows.

	We first prove that the functor is fully faithful on square-zero extensions. Let $V, W \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/ }$. By construction, $\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz}(V)) \simeq \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi (V^\vee)$ and similarly for $W$, where we write $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi (V^\vee)$ for the free $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi$-algebra on $V^\vee$. Then we have a natural map
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}} (\operatorname{sqz} (V), \operatorname{sqz}(W))  \xrightarrow{\mathfrak{D}} &  \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi (W^\vee), \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi (V^\vee)) \\
		\xrightarrow{\operatorname{forget}} & \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1] }} (\cot^\vee (\operatorname{sqz}(W)), \cot^\vee( \operatorname{sqz}(V))) \\ 
		\xrightarrow{\text{unit}_{\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi}}}  & \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}} (W^\vee, \cot^\vee (\operatorname{sqz}(V))) 
	\end{align*}
	The composition of the last two maps is an equivalence due to the free forgetful adjunction on partition Lie algebroids.
