By construction, the unit on $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi$ coincides with the unit on the adjunction $\cot^\vee : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}} \leftrightarrows (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}^{\text{op}} : \operatorname{sqz}(-)^\vee$. Hence, the composition factors as
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (\operatorname{sqz}(V), \operatorname{sqz} (W)) \xrightarrow{\cot^\vee} & \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}} (\cot^\vee(\operatorname{sqz}(W)), \cot^\vee(\operatorname{sqz}(V))) \\
		\xrightarrow{\text{unit}_{\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi}}&  \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}}(W^\vee, \cot^\vee(\operatorname{sqz}(V)))
	\end{align*}
	and it is an equivalence by the $\cot^\vee$ and $\operatorname{sqz}(-^\vee)$ adjunction. Hence, the map $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (\operatorname{sqz} (V), \operatorname{sqz} (W)) \xrightarrow{\mathfrak{D}} \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz}(W)), \mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz}(V)))$ is an equivalence.

	We will now show that if $V \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k,\geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$ is eventually coconnective, the unit map $\operatorname{sqz} (V) \to C^* (\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz} (V)))$ is an equivalence. Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}} $ be the full subcategory spanned by objects of the form $\operatorname{sqz} (V)$, where $V \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0 })_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$ is eventually coconnective, and let $\mathcal{D} \subset \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}$ be the full subcategory spanned by objects of the form $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi} (V) $ where $V \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \leq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1] /}$ is eventually coconnective. We will show that the Koszul duality adjunction restricts to an adjunction between $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}^{\text{op}}$. For this, we only need to prove that $C^* (\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz}(V))) \simeq \operatorname{sqz} (V)$. This is true by applying the Yoneda embedding to the equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (-, C^* (\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz}(V)))) & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi (V^\vee), \mathfrak{D}(-))  \\
																			& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}} (V^\vee, \cot^\vee(-)) \\
																			& \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (-, \operatorname{sqz}(V))
	\end{align*}
	We just proved that the left adjoint on $\mathcal{C}$ is fully faithful, and it is obviously essentially surjective, so the adjunction $\mathfrak{D}: \mathcal{C} \leftrightarrows \mathcal{D}^{\text{op}}: C^*$ is an equivalence. Hence, for any $X \in \mathcal{D}$, the unit $X \to \mathfrak{D}(C^* (X))$ is an equivalence.

	We will now prove the more general statement. Let $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$. Then, $A$ can be obtained as a sequence of square-zero extensions, all of which are taken to pushouts by $\mathfrak{D}$ (\cref{prop-KDpushout}). The functor $C^*$ preserves pushouts by the adjunction. Hence, the functor $C^* \circ \mathfrak{D}$ preserves all of the pullbacks in the refined Postnikov tower. This reduces it to the case $A = \operatorname{sqz} (V)$ for $V \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$, which we have already proved.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- defi-32: body_md -->
Let $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega$ and $n < 0$. The \emph{abelian partition Lie algebra on $V[n]$} is the partition Lie algebra $\operatorname{ab} (V[n]) := \mathfrak{D} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^*  (V^\vee[-n]))$.

	The category of \emph{nilpotent partition Lie algebras} is the smallest full subcategory of $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \blacksquare}$ that is closed under pullbacks and contains $\operatorname{ab}(V[n])$ for every $n \leq 0$ and $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega$. We will write $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}}$ for this category.
<!-- end defi-32 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
Let $F$ be the functor
	\begin{align*}
		F: \operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}}) \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \blacksquare}
	\end{align*}
	given by the inverse-limit-preserving extension of the fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}} \subset \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \blacksquare}$. Then, $F$ is not fully faithful.
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Let $V = \varprojlim V_i$ be a profinite vector space. Then, $F$ sends the formal inverse limit $\varprojlim \operatorname{ab} (V_i[n])$ to the partition Lie algebra $\operatorname{ab} (V[n]) \simeq \mathfrak{D} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^* (V^\vee [-n]))$. Then, we can compute the following mapping space by applying \cref{thm-Liecolim}.
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\operatorname{ab} (V[n]), \operatorname{ab} (k[0])) \simeq \varprojlim_m \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare} } (\operatorname{ab} (V[n]), \operatorname{ab} (k[0]))
	\end{align*}
	There is an equivalence of $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m}$-algebras $\operatorname{ab} (V[n]) \simeq \mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq m} (V^\vee [-n] ))$. By \cref{prop-cotcomonadic}, the functor $\mathfrak{D}^{\leq m} : \operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m} \to \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} m, \blacksquare}$ is fully faithful. Hence,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi}} (\operatorname{ab} (V[n]), \operatorname{ab} (k[0])) & \simeq \varprojlim_m \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq m}} (\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq m} (k[0]), \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq m} (V^\vee [-n])) \\
																						 & \simeq \varprojlim_m \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq m} (V^\vee [-n])
	\end{align*}
	Whereas, since $\operatorname{ab} (k[0])$ is cocompact in $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}})$,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}})} (\operatorname{ab} (V[n]), \operatorname{ab} (k[0])) & \simeq \varinjlim_i \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \operatorname{Nil}}} (\operatorname{ab} (V_i[n]), \operatorname{ab} (k[0]))  \\
																												  & \simeq \varinjlim _i \varprojlim_m \mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}^{\leq m} (V_i^\vee [-n])
	\end{align*}
	The natural map between these mapping spaces is not an isomorphism. Indeed, if $\{x_j\}_{j \in J}$ is a dual basis of $V$, the first mapping space consists of formal power series on these variables that are finite in each degree. On the other hand, the second mapping space consists of formal power series on these variables that only use finitely many variables.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- rem-26: body_md -->
However, an analogous equivalence does hold for dually truncated partition Lie algebras. This is essentially given by the equivalence $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/k}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n, \blacksquare} (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}} ) \simeq (\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n})^{\text{op}}$. The category $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}, \leq n}$ is the Ind-completion of finite colimits of finite free $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_k^{\leq n}$-algebras. By applying Koszul duality, we can write $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/ k}^{\pi, \operatorname{\substack{  _{} \vspace{-3.8pt} \\ \eqslantless }} n} (\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \leq 0}^{\operatorname{Pro}})$ as the Pro-completion of the category of finite pullbacks of finite abelian Lie algebras.
<!-- end rem-26 -->
<!-- defi-33: body_md -->
An \emph{inaccessible nilpotent formal moduli problem} is a functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $F(k) \simeq *$
		\item If $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ are $\pi_0$-surjective maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, the diagram
			\[
				\begin{tikzcd}
					F(A \times_C B) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & F(A) \arrow{d} \\
					F(B) \arrow{r} & F(C)
				\end{tikzcd}
			\]
		is a pullback square.
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-33 -->
<!-- construction-17: body_md -->
Let $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ be an inaccessible nilpotent formal moduli problem. Then, we have a functor $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{L_{k/R}[-1]} \to \mathcal{S}$ given by
	\begin{align*}
		V \mapsto F(k \oplus V[n])
	\end{align*}
	This functor preserves $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks by the assumption that $F$ is an inaccessible nilpotent formal moduli problem. We will call $T_F$ the \emph{tangent complex of $F$}.
<!-- end construction-17 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lemma-weirdKan}
	Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal, and let $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty} \subset \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}$ be the full subcategory of eventually coconnective chain complexes. Then, there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fun} _{\kappa, \pi_0} (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}, \mathcal{S}) \simeq \operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa
	\end{align*}
	where $\operatorname{Fun} _{\kappa, \pi_0} (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}, \mathcal{S}) \subset \operatorname{Fun} (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}, \mathcal{S})$ is the full subcategory of functors that commute with $\kappa$-filtered colimits and preserve $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks and the terminal object.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We will start by writing $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}$ as an accessible category. Let $\operatorname{Mod}_k^b \subset \operatorname{Mod}_k$ be the full subcategory of bounded chain complexes, and let $\operatorname{Mod}_k^{b, \kappa} \subset \operatorname{Mod}_k^b$ be the full subcategory of bounded chain complexes whose homology has dimension $< \kappa$. We will show that
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Ind} _\kappa (\operatorname{Mod}_k^{b, \kappa}) \simeq \operatorname{Mod}_k^b
	\end{align*}
	Firstly, $\operatorname{Mod}_k^b \subset \operatorname{Mod}_k$ is closed under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Suppose $F: I \to \operatorname{Mod}_k^b$ is a $\kappa$-filtered diagram. Let $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence with $x_n \in \pi_n ( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F)$. Lift each $x_n$ to an element $y_n \in \pi_n (F(i_n))$ for some $i_n \in I$. Since $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered and $\kappa$ is uncountable, the diagram consisting of the $i_n$ admits a cocone $i$. So there is a factorisation $F(i_n) \to F(i) \to  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F$. Since $F(i)$ is bounded, $x_n = 0$ for all but finitely many $n$. This shows $ 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \in \operatorname{Mod}_k^b$.

	The objects in $\operatorname{Mod}_k^{b, \kappa}$ are clearly $\kappa$-compact. By (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.3.5.11), we just need to show that the objects in $\operatorname{Mod}_k^{b, \kappa}$ generate all of $\operatorname{Mod}_k^b$ under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. But this is clear since every chain complex is split.

	By a similar argument, $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty} \simeq \operatorname{Ind}_\kappa (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa})$, where $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa} \subset \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}$ is the full subcategory of chain complexes whose homology has dimension $< \kappa$.

	By (\cite{ultrasolid}, Proposition 2.25), for an uncountable strong limit cardinal $\kappa$, we can describe $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa$ as the $\infty$-category of exact functors $(\operatorname{Solid}_{k, \geq 0}^{\operatorname{perf}, \kappa} )^{\text{op}} \to \mathcal{S}$, or equivalently, exact functors $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa} \to \mathcal{S}$, where $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa} \subset \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}$.

	Restriction gives an equivalence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa \simeq \operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{exact}} (\operatorname{Mod}_k^{b, \kappa}, \mathcal{S}) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Fun} _{\pi_0} (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa}, \mathcal{S})
	\end{align*}
	where the subscript $\pi_0$ refers to those functors preserving $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks and the terminal object. Its inverse is given by right Kan extension. 

	The result now follows, since any functor $F \in \operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal{A}, \pi_0} (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}, \mathcal{S})$ is left Kan extended from $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa}$ for some cardinal $\kappa$, and the left Kan extension of any functor $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa} \to \mathcal{S}$ that preserves $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks will also preserve $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks..
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lemma-cotcomplexasfunctor}
	Let $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_k$. Then, there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal{A}, \pi_0} ((\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{V/}, \mathcal{S}) \simeq (\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/V^\vee}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
This immediately follows from \cref{lemma-weirdKan} and (\cite{foliations}, Proposition 3.15).
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- rem-27: body_md -->
By \cref{lemma-cotcomplexasfunctor}, we can identify the category $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee[1]}$ with the category of functors $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty}) _{L_{k/R}[-1]} \to \mathcal{S}$ that are accessible and preserve $\pi_0$-surjective pullbacks; that is, they are left Kan extended from $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$ for some uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, where $\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa}$ is the category of bounded connective chain complexes whose homology has dimension $< \kappa$.
<!-- end rem-27 -->
<!-- defi-34: body_md -->
A \emph{nilpotent formal moduli problem} is an inaccessible nilpotent formal moduli problem $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ such that $T_{k/F}[1] : (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]} \to \mathcal{S}$ is an object in $(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.

	We will write $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare}$ for the $\infty$-category of nilpotent formal moduli problems.
<!-- end defi-34 -->
<!-- rem-28: body_md -->
It is not clear a priori that the category $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare}$ is locally small, but this is the case by \cref{cor-modulicolim}.
<!-- end rem-28 -->
<!-- rem-29: body_md -->
By (\cite{DAGX}, Proposition 1.1.19) and \cref{prop-smallsurjections}, a functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ preserves pullbacks of $\pi_0$-surjective morphisms if and only if it preserves pullbacks of the form
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			A \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & B \arrow{d} \\
			k \arrow{r} & k \oplus V[n]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	for $n > 0$ and $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k$.
<!-- end rem-29 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
\label{prop-accessiblefmp}
	Let $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ be a nilpotent formal moduli problem such that $T_{k/F}[1]$ is a $\lambda$-ultrasolid module for some uncountable cardinal $\lambda$. Then, $F$ commutes with all $\lambda$-filtered colimits that, when computed in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$, exist in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$.
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Let $J: I \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ be a functor, where $I$ is a $\lambda$-filtered category. Firstly, suppose that $J$ factors through the full subcategory $ \tau _{\leq 0}  \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}  \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ of $0$-truncated objects.

	Given $A \in  \tau _{\leq 0} \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, write $A_{\leq n}$ for the object $A/\mathfrak{m}^{n+1} \in  \tau _{\leq 0} \operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, where $\mathfrak{m}$ is the kernel ideal of $A$. Notice that, for all $A \in  \tau _{\leq 0} \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, $A_{\leq n} \simeq A $ for $n \gg 0$ and hence $F(A) \simeq \varprojlim F(A_{\leq n})$. This implies that $J \simeq \varprojlim J_{\leq n}$ where $J_{\leq n}$ is the functor $i \mapsto J(i)_{\leq n}$, and additionally $F \circ J \simeq \varprojlim F \circ J_{\leq n}$.

	Since $\aleph_0 < \lambda$ and $\lambda$-small limits commute with $\lambda$-filtered colimits, we may assume that $J = J_{\leq n}$ for some $n$. If $n = 0$, then $F(i) = k$ for all $i \in I$, so the statement is trivially true.

	We now proceed by induction. Suppose $n > 0$. By (\cite{HA}, Theorem 7.4.1.23) and (\cite{SAG}, Proposition 25.3.5.1), we have a pullback diagram of functors
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			J_{\leq n} 	\arrow{r} \arrow{d} & J_{\leq n-1} \arrow{d}  \\
			k \arrow{r} & k \oplus J_n[1]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where $J_n = \operatorname{fib} (J_{\leq n} \to J_{\leq n-1})$, and this fibre is computed in the category of functors $I \to \operatorname{Mod}_R$. Notice that $J_n$ can be promoted to a functor $I \to \operatorname{Mod}_k$, and its image is actually in the subcategory $\operatorname{Mod}_k^\heartsuit \subset \operatorname{Mod}_k$. Since $F$ commutes with each of these pullbacks pointwise, we have a pullback diagram of the form
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			F \circ J_{\leq n} 	\arrow{r} \arrow{d} & F \circ J_{\leq n-1} \arrow{d}  \\
			* \arrow{r} & F \circ (k \oplus J_n[1])
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	Hence, since filtered colimits commute with finite limits, 
	\begin{align*}
		F \circ  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I J_{\leq n} \simeq \operatorname{fib} (F \circ  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I J_{\leq n-1} \to F ( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I k \oplus J_n [1])) \\
	\end{align*}
	Both colimits in the fibre commute with $F$: the first one by inductive hypothesis, and the second one because $T_F$ is a $\lambda$-ultrasolid module. Finite limits commute with filtered colimits so $F \circ  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I J_{\leq n} \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \circ J_{\leq n}$ as required. 

	We will now proceed in a similar way by using refined Postnikov towers (\cref{construction-refinedPostnikov}) instead of the adic filtration. We have shown the result for when $J$ factors through $ \tau _{\leq 0} \operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{bNil}}$. For general $J$, we have an isomorphism $J \simeq \varprojlim  \tau _{\leq n} \circ J$. Given that the Postnikov tower on any element of $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{bNil}}$ is finite, $F \simeq \varprojlim F \circ \tau_{\leq n}$, and remember that Postnikov towers also commute with filtered colimits. We again apply that $\lambda$-small limits commute with $\lambda$-filtered colimits, so that we only need to show that $ \tau _{\leq n} J$ commutes with $\lambda$-filtered colimits.

	We proceed by induction on $n$. The case $n = 0$ has already been covered. Suppose $n > 0$. We now use the refined Postnikov towers to write $\tau_{\leq n} J \simeq \varprojlim_i \tau_{\leq n}^i J$, where $\tau_{\leq n}^0 \simeq \tau_{\leq n-1}$. For each element in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, this tower is finite, and the functors $\tau_{\leq n} ^i$ commute with filtered colimits, so we can repeat the previous reasoning and reduce it to showing that $\tau_{\leq n} ^i J$ commutes with $\lambda$-filtered colimits. The case $i = 0$ is handled by the inductive hypothesis on $n$. We have a pullback diagram of the form
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\tau_{\leq n}^{i+1} J \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & \tau_{\leq n}^i J \arrow{d} \\
			k \arrow{r} & k \oplus \mathfrak{m}^{i}\pi_n J/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1} [n+1]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	$F$ preserves this pullback diagram pointwise. We may repeat the same argument as when we inducted on the adic filtration, by applying the inductive hypothesis and the assumption that $F$ is a nilpotent formal moduli problem, so we are done.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- defi-35: body_md -->
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. We will write $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ for the full subcategory spanned by those $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ such that $\mathfrak{m}^j \pi_i (A)/ \mathfrak{m}^{j+1}$ has dimension less than $\kappa$ as a $k$-vector space for all $i,j$, where $\mathfrak{m}$ is the kernel ideal of $\pi_0 (A)$.
<!-- end defi-35 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lemma-IndbNil}
	If $\kappa$ is a cardinal with $\kappa > \aleph_0$, then $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k} ^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \subset \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ is closed under $\kappa$-filtered colimits.

	Additionally, there is a cardinal $\kappa_0$ such that for all cardinals $\kappa >  \kappa_0$ there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa ( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}) \simeq \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
For the first part, consider a diagram $F: I \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, where $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Then, $ 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \to k$ is $\pi_0$-surjective. Suppose, for a contradiction, that $ 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \notin \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$. Then, it is either not nilpotent or not bounded. 

	Suppose that $\pi_n (\operatorname{fib} ( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \to k)) \neq 0$ for infinitely many $n$. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, pick $x_n \in \pi_n (\operatorname{fib}( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \to k))$ such that $x_n \neq 0$ for infinitely many $n$. For each $n$, pick $i_n \in I$ and an element $y_n \in \pi_n ( \operatorname{fib} (F(i_n) \to k))$ that lifts $x_n$. Since $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered, there exists $i \in I$ such that there is a map $i_n \to i$ for all $n$. Hence, each of the maps $\operatorname{fib} (F(i_n) \to k)$ factors through $\operatorname{fib} (F(i) \to k)$. By assumption, $F(i)  \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R / /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, so $\operatorname{fib} (F(i) \to k)$ is eventually coconnective, which implies that $x_n = 0$ for $i \gg 0$, which is a contradiction.

	Alternatively, suppose that $\mathfrak{m} = \ker (\pi_0 ( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F) \to k)$ is not nilpotent. This implies that for each $n$, there exist $x_{n,1}, \dots, x_{n,n} \in \mathfrak{m}$ such that $x_{n,1} \dots  x_{n,n} \neq 0$. For each $n,j$ pick $i_{n,j} \in I$ and a lift $y_{n,j} \in \ker (\pi_0 F(i_{n,j}) \to k)$ of $x_{n,j}$. We may now pick $i \in I$ such that each map $F(i_{n,j}) \to k$ factorises through $F(i)$. Since $F(i) \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, this implies that $x_{n,1}  \dots  x_{n,n} = 0$ for $n \gg 0$, a contradiction.

	Hence, $ 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I F \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$.

	We now prove the second part. Let $\kappa_0$ be such that $k \in \operatorname{Mod}_R $ is $\kappa_0$-compact as an $R$-module. Without loss of generality, $\kappa_0 > \aleph_0$. Consider the object $k \oplus V[n]$, where $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k$ has dimension less than $\kappa$. This can be written, as an $R$-module, as a $\kappa$-small colimit of $\kappa$-compact objects, so it is $\kappa$-compact as well. Using refined Postnikov towers (\cref{construction-refinedPostnikov}), we can construct any object in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ as a finite number of pullbacks of $\kappa$-compact objects in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. Since $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ is stable, we see that for any $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$, the underlying chain complex of $A$ is $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$.

	We claim that if $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$ is $\kappa$-compact as a chain complex, then it is $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$. It suffices to show that it is $\kappa$-compact as an object in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$. We can write $A$ as its Bar resolution in $\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}$. Then,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_R^{\operatorname{an}}} (A, -) \simeq \operatorname{Tot} \operatorname{Map} _{\operatorname{Mod}_R} ((\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^* )^{\circ \bullet + 1} (A), -)
	\end{align*} 
	Since $\kappa > \aleph_0$, the $\mathbb{L}\operatorname{Sym}_R^*$ monad preserves $\kappa$-compact objects in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. Totalisations commute with $\kappa$-filtered colimits, so we see that $A$ is $\kappa$-compact. Hence, all objects in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ are $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$.

	By (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.3.5.11), there is a fully faithful embedding $\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa} (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}) \to \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}$. Since $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ is closed under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, we see that the essential image is contained in $ \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$.

	By (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.3.5.11) again, it suffices to show that $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ generates all of $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. We will proceed by induction on refined Postnikov towers.

	Let $A \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_I A_i$, where $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered and $A_i \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ for all $i$, and let $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k$. Write $V =  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 _J V_j$, where $J$ is $\kappa$-filtered and $V_j$ has dimension $< \kappa$. Suppose we have a map $A \to k \oplus V[n+1]$. It suffices to show that $A \times_{k \oplus V[n+1]} k$ can be written as a $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$.

	By the proof of (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.3.5.15), we can write this map as a colimit $ 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_L (A_l \to k \oplus V_l[n+1])$, where $L \subset I \times J$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Then, $A \times_{k \oplus V[n+1]} k \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
_L A_l \times_{k \oplus V_l [n+1]} k$.

	For all $l$, $A_l \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ and $V_l$ has dimension $< \kappa$, so $A_l \times_{k \oplus V_l [n+1]} k \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$. Hence, we see that $A \times_{k \oplus V[n+1]} k$ is a $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- example-6: body_md -->
If $\kappa = \aleph_0$, $\kappa$-filtered colimits are not well-behaved in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$. For example, set $R = k$, and we have the colimit in $\operatorname{CAlg}^{\operatorname{an}}_{k/ /k}$
	\begin{align*}
		k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2 \simeq \varinjlim_n k[x^{1/2^n}]/x^2
	\end{align*}
	where the map $k[x^{1/2^\infty}] \to k$ maps $x$ to zero. We claim that this colimit exists in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, and it is equal to $k$. 

	We will first prove that for $V \in \operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2, k \oplus V) \simeq *$, which is equivalent to $L_{k/k[x^{1/2^\infty}/x^2]} \simeq 0$.

	We can write $k[x^{1/2^n}]/x^2 \simeq k[y_n]/y_n^{2^{n+1}}$, where $y_n^{2^n} = x$. We have a derived pushout
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			k[y_n ^{2^{n+1}}] \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & k[y_n] \arrow{d} \\
			k \arrow{r} & k[y_n]/y_n^{2^{n+1}}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The map $k[x^{1/2^n}]/x^2 \to k[x^{1/2^{n+1}}]/x^2$ is induced by the map $y_n \mapsto y_{n+1}^2$, Since the cotangent complex commutes with colimits,
	\begin{align*}
		L_{k/k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2} \simeq \operatorname{cofib}( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 L_{k/k[y_n^{2^{n+1}}]} \to  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 L_{k/k[y_n]})
	\end{align*}
	Remember that $L_{k/k[z]} \simeq k[1]$, and a squaring map between polynomial algebras in one generator induces a trivial map in $\cot$. Hence, both elements in the cofibre are zero, and $\cot(k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2) \simeq 0$.

	Now suppose we have a cocone for the above colimit in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ with vertex $R$. Then, it factors through $k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2$. Writing $R$ as a finite pullback of square-zero extensions, we see that $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}^{\operatorname{an}}_{k/ /k}} (k[x^{1/2^\infty}]/x^2, R) \simeq *$. Hence, the cocone factorises through $k$, which is initial and final in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$, so the cone must be trivial. We conclude that the colimit of this diagram in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{k/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ exists and is equal to $k$.
<!-- end example-6 -->
<!-- defi-36: body_md -->
A \emph{$\kappa$-small nilpotent formal moduli problem} is a functor $F: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa} \to \mathcal{S}$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $F(k) \simeq *$.
		\item If $A \to C$ and $B \to C$ are $\pi_0$-surjective maps in $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$, the diagram
			\[
				\begin{tikzcd}
					F(A \times_C B) \arrow{r} \arrow{d} & F(A) \arrow{d} \\
					F(B) \arrow{r} & F(C)
				\end{tikzcd}
			\]
		is a pullback square.
	\end{enumerate}
	We will write $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa}$ for the $\infty$-category of $\kappa$-small ultrasolid formal moduli problems.
<!-- end defi-36 -->
<!-- construction-18: body_md -->
Given $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa}$, we will still write 
	\begin{align*}
		T_{k/F}[1] : (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/} \to \mathcal{S}
	\end{align*}
	for the functor
	\begin{align*}
		(L_{k/R}[-1] \xrightarrow{\alpha} V) \mapsto F(k \oplus_\alpha V)
	\end{align*}
	By \cref{lemma-cotcomplexasfunctor}, we can identify $T_{k/F}[1]$ with an object in $(\operatorname{Solid}_k^\kappa)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}$.
<!-- end construction-18 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\label{prop-smallfmp}
	Let $\kappa > \kappa_0$, where $\kappa_0$ is the cardinal in \cref{lemma-IndbNil}, be an infinite strong limit cardinal. Then, left Kan extension gives a fully faithful embedding
	\begin{align*}
		\Phi: \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa} \to \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare
	\end{align*}
	Additionally, $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$ is in the image of this embedding if and only if the tangent complex $T_{k/F}$ is $\kappa$-ultrasolid.
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- rem-30: body_md -->
Using the above, from now on we will identify $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa}$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$ as described above.
<!-- end rem-30 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Left Kan extension gives a fully faithful embedding
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa} \to \operatorname{Fun}_\kappa (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}, \mathcal{S})
	\end{align*}
	where $\operatorname{Fun}_\kappa (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}, \mathcal{S}) \subset \operatorname{Fun} (\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}, \mathcal{S})$ is the full subcategory of $\kappa$-filtered-colimit-preserving functors (\cref{lemma-IndbNil} and \cite{HTT}, Lemma 5.3.5.8). So we just need to check that if $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa}$, its left Kan extension $\Phi (F) : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \mathcal{S}$ is a nilpotent formal moduli problem. Given a pullback diagram of the form
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			A	\arrow{r} \arrow{d} & B \arrow{d} \\
			k \arrow{r} & k \oplus V[n]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where $A \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}}$ and $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k$, we must show that it is preserved by $\Phi(F)$.

	By (\cite{HTT}, Proposition 5.3.5.15), the map $B \to k \oplus V[n]$ can be written as a $\kappa$-filtered colimit of maps of the form $B_i \to k \oplus V_i[n]$, where $B_i \in \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ and $V_i \in \operatorname{Vect}_k$ has dimension $< \kappa$. Since $\Phi(F)$ commutes with $\kappa$-filtered colimits and finite limits commute with filtered colimits,
	\begin{align*}
		\Phi(F)(A) & \simeq \Phi(F)( 
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 B_i \times _{k \oplus V_i[n]} k) \\
				  & \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 F(B_i \times_{k \oplus V_i[n]} k) \\
				  & \simeq  
  \mathop{\mathpalette\colim@{\scriptscriptstyle}}\nmlimits@
 F(B_i) \times _{F(k \oplus V_i[n])} * \\
				  & \simeq \Phi(F)(B) \times _{\Phi(F)(k \oplus V[n])} *
	\end{align*}
	This shows $\Phi(F) \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$.

	We now show the last part. Suppose $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$ such that $T_{k/F}[1] $ is $\kappa$-ultrasolid. Then, by \cref{prop-accessiblefmp}, $F$ commutes with $\kappa$-filtered colimits, so $F$ is left Kan extended from $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$ (\cite{HTT}, Lemma 5.3.5.8). 

	Conversely, if $F$ is left Kan extended from $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \kappa}$, it commutes with $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Then, $T_{k/F}[1] : (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{L_{k/R}[-1] /} \to \mathcal{S}$ commutes with $\kappa$-filtered colimits, so it is left Kan extended from $(\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty, \kappa})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$. Thus, $T_{k/F}[1]$ is $\kappa$-ultrasolid (\cref{lemma-cotcomplexasfunctor}).
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor-modulicolim}
	There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare} \simeq \varinjlim _\kappa \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \kappa}
	\end{align*}
	where the colimit is taken over all uncountable strong limit cardinals $\kappa$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
This follows from \cref{prop-smallfmp}, since for any $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare$, its tangent complex $T_F$ is $\kappa$-ultrasolid for some $\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- prop-25: body_md -->
\label{prop-deftheory}
	Let $\sigma$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}$, the functor $\mathfrak{D}_\sigma: \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}} \to \left(  \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \right) ^{\text{op}}$ and the set of spectrum objects $\left\{\{k \oplus V[n]\}_{n > 0} | V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k^\sigma\right\}$ are a deformation theory in the sense of (\cite{DAGX}, Definition 1.3.9).
<!-- end prop-25 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}$ be the full subcategory spanned by the image of $\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}$ under $\mathfrak{D}_\sigma$. We need to check conditions (D1)-(D4) of (\cite{DAGX}, Definition 1.3.1 and Definition 1.3.9).

	Firstly, the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}$ is presentable (\cite{monads}, Corollary 6.8). By \cref{construction-smallKD}, $\mathfrak{D}_\sigma$ has a right adjoint $C^*_\sigma : (\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma})^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{CAlg}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{surj}}_{R/ /k}$. This verifies (D1) and (D2).

	By the proof of \cref{prop-KDfullyfaithful}, the Koszul duality adjunction restricts to an adjoint equivalence $\mathfrak{D}_\sigma : \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma} \leftrightarrows \mathcal{D}^{\text{op}} : C^*$. It follows that for any $\mathfrak{g} \in \mathcal{D}$ the unit map $\mathfrak{g} \to \mathfrak{D}_\sigma(C_\sigma^* (\mathfrak{g}))$ is an equivalence. This verifies (D3).

	To each spectrum object $\{k \oplus V[n]\}_{n > 0}$ where $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k^{\sigma}$, we have a functor $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \to \operatorname{Sp}$ as follows: given $\mathfrak{g} \in \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}$, the collection of spaces $\{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}} (\mathfrak{D} (k \oplus V[n]), \mathfrak{g}) \}_{n > 0}$ forms a spectrum. Additionally, $\mathfrak{D}(k \oplus V[n]) \simeq \operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi ( V \xrightarrow{0} L_{k/R}^\vee [1] )$, so we can identify this spectrum with $\operatorname{Map}^s _{\operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma} (V^\vee,	\operatorname{fib}( \mathfrak{g} \to L_{k/R}^\vee [1] ))$, the mapping spectrum in the stable category $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma$. If we consider $\operatorname{fib} (\mathfrak{g} \to L_{k/R}^\vee [1]) \in \operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma$ as a functor $(\operatorname{Pro} (\operatorname{Vect}_k^\omega)_{< \sigma} )^{\text{op}} \to \operatorname{Sp}$, this mapping spectrum is just $\operatorname{fib} (\mathfrak{g} \to L_{k/R}^\vee [1]) (V^\vee)$.

	The monad $\operatorname{Lie}_{\Delta, k/R}^\pi$ commutes with sifted colimits, and colimits of ultrasolid modules are computed pointwise, so the functor $\mathfrak{g} \mapsto \operatorname{fib} (\mathfrak{g} \to L_{k/R}^\vee [1]) (V^\vee)$ commutes with sifted colimits. Additionally, the collection of these functors (where we take all $V \in \operatorname{Vect}_k^{\sigma}$) detects equivalences. This is because a map of partition Lie algebroids is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence of the underlying ultrasolid modules, and a map of $\sigma$-ultrasolid modules is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence at every section. This verifies (D4) and we are done.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor-smallLP}
	Let $\sigma$ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. Then, there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{theorem-nilpotentLP}
	The tangent complex $T_{k/-}: \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^\blacksquare \to \operatorname{Solid}_k$ lifts to an equivalence of $\infty$-categories 
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare} \simeq \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
We just need to check that the equivalence $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \simeq \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma}$ in \cref{cor-smallLP} is compatible with the filtered colimits $\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare} \simeq \varinjlim_\sigma \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}$ and $\operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare} \simeq \varinjlim_\sigma \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma}$ (\cref{cor-modulicolim}).

	For an uncountable strong limit cardinal $\sigma$, by the proof of (\cite{DAGX}, Theorem 1.3.12), the equivalence of $\infty$-categories
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \xrightarrow{\Psi_\sigma} \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma}
	\end{align*}
	is given by $\Psi_\sigma(\mathfrak{g}) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\mathfrak{D}_\sigma(-), \mathfrak{g}) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}}} (C^*_\sigma(\mathfrak{g}), -) \in \operatorname{Fun} ( \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}, \mathcal{S})$. For $\sigma < \sigma'$, we get a square
	\[
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma} \arrow{d} \arrow{r}{\Psi_\sigma} & \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma} \arrow{d}{\Phi_\sigma^{\sigma'}} \\
			\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma'} \arrow{r}{\Psi_{\sigma'}} & \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma'}
		\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	where the left vertical arrow is given by the fully faithful inclusion $\operatorname{Solid}_k^\sigma \subset \operatorname{Solid}_k^{\sigma'}$, and the functor $\Phi_\sigma^{\sigma'}$ is left Kan extension (\cref{prop-smallfmp}) and it is fully faithful. Thus, it suffices to show that this diagram is commutative.

	Given $F \in \operatorname{Moduli}_{R/k}^{\blacksquare, \sigma}$, $\Phi_\sigma^{\sigma'} (F)$ is the left Kan extension of $F$.	Let $\mathfrak{g} \in \operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare, \sigma}$. Then, $\mathfrak{D}_\sigma | _{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}} \simeq \mathfrak{D}_{\sigma'}|_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}}$ (\cref{lemma-smallKD}), so 
	\begin{align*}
		\Phi_\sigma^{\sigma'} (\Psi_\sigma (\mathfrak{g})) |_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}} & \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\mathfrak{D}_\sigma (-), \mathfrak{g}) \\
		&  \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\mathfrak{D}_{\sigma'} (-), \mathfrak{g})  \\
		& \simeq \Psi_{\sigma'} (\mathfrak{g})|_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}}
	\end{align*}
	Thus, it suffices to show that $\Psi_{\sigma'} (\mathfrak{g})$ is left Kan extended from $ \operatorname{CAlg}_{R/ /k}^{\operatorname{an}, \operatorname{bNil}, \sigma}$. By \cref{prop-accessiblefmp}, it suffices to check that the tangent complex of $\Psi_{\sigma'} (\mathfrak{g})$ is $\sigma$-ultrasolid. By construction, the tangent complex of $\Psi_{\sigma'}(\mathfrak{g})$ is the underlying chain complex of $\mathfrak{g}$, which is $\sigma$-ultrasolid, so the result follows.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- rem-31: body_md -->
We can easily check that, given a formal moduli problem $F$, with associated partition Lie algebroid $\mathfrak{g}$, the underlying chain complex of $\mathfrak{g}$ is precisely $T_{k/F}[1]$, as stated in the theorem. Indeed, we can write $F = \Psi (\mathfrak{g})$, and then for $V \in (\operatorname{Mod}_{k, \geq 0}^{< \infty})_{L_{k/R}[-1]/}$,
	\begin{align*}
		\Psi(\mathfrak{g}) (\operatorname{sqz} (V)) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LieAlgd}_{\Delta, k/R}^{\pi, \blacksquare}} (\mathfrak{D} (\operatorname{sqz} (V)), \mathfrak{g}) \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{(\operatorname{Solid}_k)_{/L_{k/R}^\vee [1]}} (V^\vee, \mathfrak{g})
	\end{align*}
	where we used that $\mathfrak{D}(\operatorname{sqz} (V))$ is the free partition Lie algebroid on $V^\vee$.
<!-- end rem-31 -->
